summary:
Gap map for whitepaper §4 (protocol diagrams) and §7 (refined semantic sorts), checked against the code at HEAD 9ffdf77. Bottom line: neither section is implemented as the whitepaper describes. M0 and M1 got the predicted outcomes by hand-authoring per-milestone fact documents and law IR files. What the whitepaper calls a diagram, an evidence calculus, sort inference or sorts-as-types does not exist in the code.

(1) There is no diagram object. There are three separate fact documents in two DSLs: facts/morph_header.json (holon-facts/0.1, codec functions of kind encoder/predicate/decoder/projection), spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json and spec/M1/facts/morph_batchdata.json (holon-facts/0.2 guarded-command machines). They share no carriers and are not linked: the M1 rollup models a header as a list of Nat tokens and never uses the M0 Hdr codec. There is no holon/diagram/. A grep for carrier/edge/graph/cycle/spanning over holon/ hits only a docstring in holon/gen/model.py. The edge-kind vocabulary CODEC/HASH/STORE/LOAD/CONS/TRANS/MIG/SYM appears nowhere, and schemas/facts.schema.json covers only the 0.1 M0 subset.

(2) The evidence calculus E1-E6 is not computed. Each law JSON carries a hand-written `evidence` array. It is metadata that is deliberately not hashed (ir.HASHED_KEYS; the frozen test tests/test_11_ir.py::test_hash_ignores_metadata_but_not_statement asserts this), and no code reads it. L_sort_remaining and L_tag_BVH claim E5 ("identical refined sorts") although no sorts exist. Intent-question triage comes from a hand-written config/triage.json keyed by law id. Otherwise every law defaults to "finding", whatever its evidence.

(3) There are no refined sorts. Every M1 register is Nat/Bool/List or a record of those. machine.ex compiles "-" to truncated Nat.sub after checking only that both operands are Nat. The rollup facts contain 14 subtraction sites. Only the realize site at Rollup.sol:363, which appears 3 times (once per commit action, reason 16), and the idx-1 site at :636 (reason 41) are covered, and both by hand-written requires. The other sites (`btot - bn`, `idx - lfi`, the lci/w/bvh_at/tag_at defs) produce no obligation.

(4) There is no sort inference: no constraints, no union-find, no unsat cores, no cross-component equations. z3 is not installed.

(5) Sign obligations are not proof arguments. L_sort_remaining is a hand-written trace law, `no_code(obs(p from s0), 16) == true`. It is REFUTED correctly at t = s+W+1 and replays as Panic 0x11. But it is a revert-reachability law that depends on the fact author having modelled checked arithmetic as a require. One law covers all three sites, so a failure is not localized to one site (Thm 6.18). The facts' `site: {rule: SORT, kind: realize}` annotations are read by no code. The `sort_coercion` proof class promised in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's M1 plan does not exist in holon/gen/mproofs.py.

(6) The one union, BVH (versioned hash vs aggregate), is handled by hand. The facts declare a ghost `tag` field and an `s_tag` shadow, and compute tag values in hand-written lets. The generator has a Morph-specific builtin `b_tags_exact` (version 2 iff tag 2) hard-coded at machine.py:529. `Machine.ghost_state` is loaded at machine.py:259 and never used, so nothing checks that ghost fields stay ghost. L_tag_BVH is a global invariant over committed entries, not a per-read-site `as_member` coercion.

(7) Refinement records exist only as per-action agree/disagree counts (replay/M1/report.json refinement.per_action). Disagreements are not classified, there is no per-edge mutation adequacy, and certificates do not list the refinement records of the edges they use: results say replay `not_run`.

(8) There is no inductive Reach predicate. Reachability is expressed operationally as runs from s0, or laws are proved from every state.

Reusable pieces:
- the base-typed facts DSL compiler (holon/gen/machine.py);
- the layout algebra (holon/layout.py), usable to derive E1;
- proof arguments typed as equalities, already accepted by Bend 2.0.36 in the mproofs core lemmas, so `realize(d, {is_nonneg(d) == True{} : Bool})` can be written without holes;
- record types as nominal wrappers;
- the per-action replay harness;
- the mutation harness.

Constraints on new work: AGENTS.md forbids adding files under schemas/, tests/, facts/ and laws/M0. New schemas therefore go under holon/diagram/ or holon/sorts/, new tests under a new tests_m2/, and frozen sort assignments in laws/<M>/REGISTRY.json for M2 and later.

items.item: Unified protocol diagram object 𝔇 = (V_rep, E_rep, {S_k}, {A_k}, M, 𝔉, Cm, Cn, Π, cost)
items.evidence: No holon/diagram/ (ls fails); `grep -rni 'spanning|fundamental|cycle|graph|carrier|edge' holon/` hits only the holon/gen/model.py docstring. The facts are three separate documents: facts/morph_header.json (holon-facts/0.1: keys facts_version,target,extraction,types,functions,assumptions), spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json and spec/M1/facts/morph_batchdata.json (holon-facts/0.2: state/actions/migrations/observers/consumers). schemas/facts.schema.json is titled 'holon-facts/0.1, M0 subset' and has properties only [facts_version, functions]. The M1 rollup represents a header as Nat tokens (machine.py b_hdr_of: [ver,tot,n,hb,prev,post,lbn]) and never references the M0 Hdr codecs.
items.gap: The whitepaper makes the diagram the single object that rules, basis reduction, evidence and sort inference run over. The code has only per-milestone fact documents. They share no representation layer, versioned state carriers, symmetry families, commitment set or consumer set. 𝔉 and Cm are absent entirely. Cn has one entry (consumers.blobs_of). Π is a free-text map (principals {'1':'owner',...}).
items.proposed_work:
1. Create holon/diagram/{__init__.py, model.py, build.py, diagram.schema.json}. model.py holds frozen dataclasses: Carrier(id, cls in {rep,state,env,digest}, base_type, sort_ref, interface: bool, reach), Edge(id, kind in {CODEC,HASH,STORE,LOAD,CONS,TRANS,MIG,SYM}, src, tgt, component, version, interp_ref, plus TRANS extras), and Diagram(V_rep, E_rep, S[k], A[k], M, F, Cm, Cn, Pi, cost).
2. build.py builds a Diagram deterministically from every fact document of a milestone. Adapters: facts 0.1 functions become CODEC edges over Header/Bytes; facts 0.2 actions become TRANS, migrations become MIG, consumers become CONS, state fields become STORE/LOAD pairs. It emits gen/<M>/diagram.json with sorted keys and canonical JSON.
3. Add a `python -m holon diagram --milestone M` subcommand in holon/__main__.py.
4. Gate G1 regenerates diagram.json byte-identically. Put tests in a new tests_m2/test_diagram.py (tests/ is frozen).
5. Later, extraction frontends (M2) target the diagram schema directly instead of the facts DSL.

items.item: Carrier triple (⟦v⟧, R_v, σ_v) and carrier classes (representation / state / environment / digest)
items.evidence: Value sets exist as Bend types: M0 has Hdr and Bytes = List<&2,U32> (holon/gen/model.py BEND_TYPE). M1 state fields are typed Nat/Bool/List/records (morph_rollup.json 'state', 22 entries). Environment carriers are encoded ad hoc: time is a state field 't' ('block.timestamp (environment)') advanced by the 'wait' action; the caller is an input 'who: Nat'; attached value is an input 'value' on challengeState; blobs are an input list. Digests are Nat tokens (abstractions[0]). The facts have no carrier-class field, no σ_v anywhere, and no R_v beyond 'runs from s0' in trace laws.
items.gap: Carriers carry no class and no refined sort. Reachable subsets are not attached to carriers. Header bytes over-approximate R by ranging over all byte values (ARCHITECTURE §5, L2).
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/diagram/build.py, classify each carrier: state fields become state, `wait`-driven fields and action inputs named in an env list become env, outputs of HASH edges become digest, codec inputs and outputs become rep.
2. Attach `sort_ref`, pointing into the frozen sort assignment (see the §7.7/§7.8 items), and `reach` (s0 plus TRANS edges for state; full input type for interfaces; ABI range for scalars).
3. Add an optional `class` field to facts 0.2 state entries in spec/<M>/facts. Do not edit the frozen facts/morph_header.json; derive its classes in the adapter instead.

items.item: Records as product carriers; field projections belong to the product structure, not edges
items.evidence: M1 records (Entry, BD, Ch) compile to product types with generated getters g_<Ty>_<f> (machine.py gen_types). M0 Header is a product type Hdr with get_<field> defs. However, M0 facts declare `view` as a fact function of kind 'projection' (facts.KIND_TYPES), so a projection is treated as a function/edge.
items.gap: Nothing marks projections as structural, so a future basis reduction would count them as edges and inflate |E|.
items.proposed_work: In holon/diagram/build.py, map kind 'projection' and generated getters to product-structure metadata on the carrier, not to Edge objects. Add a tests_m2 assertion that no Edge has kind projection.

items.item: Interface carriers with external reachable set R^ext (everything any principal can place there)
items.evidence: L_dom_hdr (laws/M0/L_dom_hdr.json) quantifies over all Bytes, which matches §8.3's 'R^ext = full input type' for one interface. Nothing marks a carrier as an interface. In M1, headers are presented honestly (morph_rollup.json abstractions[1]: a fabricated header 'only reaches the checks the model encodes for indices > LCI'), so the commit-path R^ext for calldata headers is not represented.
items.gap: Domain coherence ('all decoders at every interface carrier have equal domains on R^ext') cannot be generated, because no interface carriers are identified. Only the one hand-written M0 law exists.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add `interface: true` on diagram carriers reachable from external calldata or the wire. Derive it from facts: action inputs of type Bytes, M0 functions with from=Bytes.
2. Add holon/diagram/interfaces.py that enumerates, for each interface carrier, every CODEC/predicate edge with that carrier as source. The rule generator (other area) then emits one PAR-domain law per decoder pair.
3. For M1, add an optional `fabricated_header` input mode to the facts DSL so that R^ext includes non-stored headers.

items.item: Edge kinds CODEC, HASH, STORE, LOAD, CONS, TRANS, MIG, SYM with component and version labels
items.evidence: `grep -rn 'CODEC|STORE|LOAD|TRANS|"MIG"' holon spec facts schemas` finds nothing; 'SYM' appears only as a rule name. M0 function kinds are encoder/predicate/decoder/projection (holon/facts.py KIND_TYPES). M1 has actions (TRANS-like), migrations {legacy, eta2} (MIG-like) and consumers {blobs_of} (CONS-like). There are no HASH edges: M0 assumption A-hash says 'no hash premises are needed in M0', and M1 abstractions[2] drops committedBatches under CF. There are no STORE/LOAD edges, because registers are record fields, and no SYM generators g_S/g_In. Components are implicit only: M0 'lang' (solidity-evm-memory / go-bytes) and M1 'src' paths. There are no version labels: M1 models a single version and represents pre-v2 state with a 'legacy' migration effect.
items.gap: The kind taxonomy the rules dispatch on (invertible fragment, UNDO pairs via STORE/LOAD, FACT via HASH plus CONS) is absent. Component and version labels are not machine-readable.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/diagram/build.py, map each fact construct to an Edge kind and record component (from lang, or from the contract/package in src) and version (from encoder version guards, or an explicit `version` on facts 0.2 actions).
2. Add a `hash_edges` section to the facts 0.2 DSL: {name, from, to, src} compiled to an opaque parameter (see the Def 4.4 item).
3. Add `sym_generators` in facts: {family in tau/iota/pi/mu/omega, g_S, g_In} compiled by machine.py to g_S/g_In defs.
4. Make STORE/LOAD edges implicit, one pair per state field, with writer and reader actions taken from effects and guard free variables.

items.item: Edge interpretation: partial function (definedness explicit) or relation for TRANS
items.evidence: M0: undefined bytes are 0xDEAD (holon/facts.py UNDEF = 57005), and dec_go returns Maybe (holon/gen/model.py MAYBE_FIELDS). M1: every action is decide/exec with revert as the result variant O_Rev{code} (machine.py docstring; gen/M1/model/morph_rollup.bend `type HObs`). TRANS nondeterminism is resolved by explicit inputs (HAct constructors).
items.gap: None for the current scope. Bytes are not length-indexed (§8.3 says 'byte strings as length-indexed types'); that is a minor divergence handled by explicit length checks.
items.proposed_work: No new mechanism. When the diagram builder lands, record `partial: true/false` per edge from whether its Bend result type is Maybe/O_Rev or the 0xDEAD convention.

items.item: TRANS edge annotations: principal class, guard, cost term, index-sensitive read and write sets
items.evidence: Guards: done; every action has an ordered `guards` list with src lines (morph_rollup.json actions[*].guards). Principal: free-text strings ('active submitter', 'anyone (through the messenger; ...)'), with permission encoded as a guard require on `who`. Cost: disch.cost holds per-action constants {sendMessage:1, commitBatchWithProof:1000} and no state-dependent cost term (loop bounds, gas). Read sets: Machine.gen_action computes `reads` as state field names among the guards' free variables (machine.py ~568). Write sets are the effect keys. Both are field-level: `win`, `chs`, `fsr` are read or written as whole lists, with no symbolic index.
items.gap: The whitepaper requires index-sensitive read and write sets (needed by UNDO deadness §10.6 and DISCH Write*_X). It also requires a typed principal class with a permission predicate, and cost_a(s,x) as a term usable in En_G(s).
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/gen/machine.py, add an index-sensitive access analysis. For list-valued fields, record the index expression of each nth/w/bvh_at/set_* call, e.g. (win, idx-lfi), (chs, bc), and emit `access` JSON into gen/<M>/diagram.json per action.
2. Replace the free-text principal with `principal: {class: <role>, pred: <expr>}` in facts 0.2. machine.py emits `perm_<a>(who, s)`, and the decide chain uses it.
3. Add a `cost` expression per action in facts (default constant), compiled to `cost_<a>(s, in) -> Nat`.

items.item: Invertible vs lossy fragments; HASH edges invertible only under local CF premises
items.evidence: No injectivity classification anywhere (grep 'injective|invertible|lossy' over holon/ finds nothing relevant). M1 replaces keccak over blob hashes with a concrete injective stand-in, the `agg` builtin (machine.py ~311: Nat.add(AGG_BASE, b_enc(xs)), with b_enc a Cantor-pairing encoding). abstractions[5] says this 'models CF(keccak256, S) for every finite S'. Laws are therefore instantiated at one injective function, not parametric in h with a CF(h,S) premise.
items.gap: There is no fragment classification for basis reduction. HASH edges are concrete injective functions rather than opaque parameters `h` with visible CF(h, S) premises (diverging from §8.3/§8.5 and Cor 6.16).
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/diagram/fragments.py. A CODEC edge is invertible iff layout.py shows every field position is recoverable (getter recovery per §10.2). A decoder is invertible iff its domain guard is total on R_src. HASH edges are invertible-under-CF and record the finite term set S used by each law. Everything else is lossy.
2. Emit the result in diagram.json.
3. In machine.py, compile hash_edges as a module-level parameter, e.g. `def step(h: List<&2,Nat> -> Nat, ...)`, or as an extra HSt field holding an oracle table, together with an emitted CF premise binder.
4. Keep `agg` only as the replay-side concretization.

items.item: Evidence calculus: compute the highest evidence level E1-E6 for each pair of parallel paths
items.evidence: Evidence is hand-written metadata on each law: laws/M0/*.json, e.g. L_par_hdr_v2 ['E1','E6'], and laws/M1/*.json, e.g. L_sort_remaining ['E5'], L_tag_BVH ['E2','E5']. ir.py HASHED_KEYS excludes it, and the frozen tests/test_11_ir.py::test_hash_ignores_metadata_but_not_statement asserts that editing evidence leaves the hash unchanged. `grep -rn evidence holon/` finds only the ir.py docstring: no code reads or computes it. E5 ('identical refined sorts') is claimed although no sort assignment exists. Parallel paths are not enumerated.
items.gap: Evidence levels are assertions by the law author, not derived from the diagram. The strong/medium/weak distinction cannot gate which obligations become defects, and the §13 ablation 'no evidence calculus' cannot be run.
items.depends_on: §4 Def 4.3 diagram object; §7.7 sort inference (for E5)

items.item: Strong/medium evidence yields defects; weak (E6-only) evidence yields intent questions
items.evidence: Triage comes from config/triage.json keyed by law id (M0: L_par_hdr_ssvh → 'intent_question', although its law metadata says ['E1']; M1: three entries). holon/pipeline.py:166-167 and holon/mpipeline.py:289-290 default every refuted law to 'finding', whatever its evidence.
items.gap: Triage is hand-assigned per law id, not derived from the evidence level, so a weak-evidence refutation would be reported as a defect.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/pipeline.py and holon/mpipeline.py, compute the default triage from gen/<M>/evidence.json: a max level of E6 gives 'intent_question'; E1-E5 give 'finding'.
2. Keep config/triage.json only as an override that must carry `why` and `evidence_override: true`, and report overrides in the gate report.
3. Add a tests_m2 test that a synthetic E6-only law is triaged as an intent question.

items.item: Morph diagram excerpt coverage: codecs, payload and derivation pipelines, commitments, transitions, migrations, symmetry families
items.gap: The diagram covers the M0/M1 slice only. Appendix B's carriers and edges for the payload and derivation pipelines, the commitments, the other four migrations and three symmetry families are absent.
items.proposed_work:
1. As M2 extraction lands (solc/Yul → facts, go/ssa → facts), add spec/M3/facts/ documents for the payload pipeline codecs (Go), derivation (Go), the messenger and registry (Solidity), and migrations η₃/η₄/η_enq/η_BVH. Each carries source lines.
2. Link them through the diagram builder (§4 Def 4.3) with linking equations (§7.7 step 5).
3. Track coverage as diagram edges present vs Appendix B, written to gen/<M>/coverage.json.
items.depends_on: §4 Def 4.3 diagram object; M2 extraction frontends

items.item: Executable model 𝔅(𝔇): one type per carrier, one function per edge or transition, inductive reachability predicate per state carrier
items.evidence: holon/gen/machine.py emits HSt, HEntry, HBD, HCh, HObs and HAct, plus decide_<a>/exec_<a>/step_<a> per action. holon/gen/model.py emits one def per M0 fact function. There is no Reach predicate: `grep -rn Reach holon/ schemas/` finds nothing. docs/M1_REPORT.md §7 says D4 invariants 'need induction over Reach'. Laws instead hold from every state (L_undo_*) or over traces from s0 (`{run: p, from: {s0: {}}}`). The docs/ARCHITECTURE.md M1 plan item 3 promised `Reach` as an inductive predicate.
items.gap: There is no inductive `Reach : S → Type`, so invariant laws over reachable states (D4, L2 remedy) cannot be stated or proved. There is one type per record, not one per refined sort.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/gen/machine.py, emit `type Reach(s: HSt) is Type: R0{} : Reach(s0()) | RStep{a: HAct, r: Reach(s)} : Reach(step(a, s))`, adapted to Bend 2's indexed-type syntax per docs/bend_guide.txt. Verify it with a probe outside bend/probes/ (frozen), e.g. build/probes/.
2. Add an IR 0.3 binder type `ReachState` in holon/gen/mlaws.py that binds (s, r: Reach(s)).
3. Add a proof generator `reach_induction` in holon/gen/mproofs.py: the invariant is preserved by each step lemma and holds at s0.
4. Ship it with a law for D4: P = total(h_LFI) ≤ T ≤ L.

items.item: Refinement record ρ(e) per edge: implementation reference, replay corpus, agreement count, classified disagreements, mutation-adequacy results
items.evidence: replay/M1/report.json has refinement.per_action agree/disagree counts per action (e.g. commitBatch 874/0), plus seed 20261011, 300 traces, 2432 steps, and a disagreements list (empty). Implementation references exist as 'src' per action and guard in the facts. Disagreements are collected but not classified (holon/mreplay.py:382-392 only counts them; no extraction-defect / real-defect / oracle-mismatch labels). Mutation adequacy is global (spec/M1/mutations.json, tests_m1/test_m1_mutations.py), not per edge. M0 CODEC edges have only witness replay (replay/M0/report.json), with no per-edge corpus.
items.gap: There is no per-edge record object. Disagreements are unclassified. Mutation adequacy is not attributed to edges. CODEC edges have no agreement volume.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/refinement.py that writes results/<M>/refinement/<edge_id>.json with {edge, impl_ref (file:lines from facts src), corpus (seed, n, hash), agree, disagree, disagreements: [{input, model, real, class}], mutations: [{id, killed}]}.
2. Add a classification step in holon/mreplay.py: disagreements on oracle stand-in calls become oracle_mismatch, reproducible on a real-code-only rerun become real_defect, everything else becomes extraction_defect pending review.
3. Make the mutation runner record which edge each mutation touches; the facts JSON pointer gives the action.
4. Add a per-codec corpus driver for M0 CODEC edges in holon/replay.py.

items.item: Certificate scope lists the refinement records of every edge its proof uses
items.evidence: The result record's replay field is fixed at {status: 'not_run', detail: 'certificates are not replayed; refinement replay corpus in replay/M1'} (holon/mpipeline.py:237; holon/pipeline.py:154 for M0). No edge-use computation exists for laws.
items.gap: Certificates do not state which edges, and hence which refinement evidence, they rely on, so 'certified absent relative to 𝔇 with this refinement evidence' (§12.1) is not reported.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/mpipeline.py, compute `edges_used` per law from the Bend call graph of the LAWS.bend claim: Trace binders use all TRANS edges; observer and migration calls use their defs. Use the generated model's def dependency graph from machine.py.
2. Attach [{edge, refinement_sha256}] to each result record.
3. Gate G9 (records complete) requires the field.

items.item: Refined sort grammar: Mach(w) | Time | Dur^± | Idx[κ] | Cnt[κ]^± | Prin[role] | Amt[asset] | Dig[kind] | Ver | Bool | σ₁+σ₂ | ⟨fields⟩
items.evidence: `grep -rn 'Time\b|SDur|Dur\b|IdxFin|IdxInc|time_sub|realize|as_member'` over holon/ finds none (the hits are Python's time module). M1 state types are only Nat/Bool/List<..>/records (morph_rollup.json 'state'). M0 header fields carry byte widths plus informal strings such as 'BatchIndex uint64'. The only sort-like text is the unread facts annotation "sort": "Dur(signed) realized in uint256" (morph_rollup.json lines ~1114, ~1506, ~2021). The facts DSL has base typing only: Machine.ex raises FactsError on non-Nat arithmetic.
items.gap: There is no sort language, so there is nothing to infer, assign, freeze or compile.
items.proposed_work:
1. Create holon/sorts/{__init__.py, grammar.py}: frozen dataclasses for each sort constructor, a parser and printer for the textual form (e.g. 'Idx[queue]_inc', 'Dur^±'), canonical JSON, and a total order for deterministic output.
2. Add holon/sorts/sorts.schema.json; schemas/ is frozen, so it cannot go there.
3. Unit tests in tests_m2/test_sorts_grammar.py.

items.item: Affine rules (Time/Dur and Idx/Cnt torsors, ill-sorted combinations) and automatic sign-obligation generation for signed sorts realized in unsigned arithmetic
items.gap: Sign obligations are not generated from the arithmetic. They exist only where a human modelled checked arithmetic. Ill-sorted expressions such as Time+Time or mixing index families are not detected.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/sorts/check.py, a sort checker over the facts 0.2 expression language that mirrors Machine.ex. Inputs are the frozen assignment and the operator table from §7.2. For each '-' or '+' site, compute the result sort. A signed result (Dur^±, Cnt^±, Idx^±) consumed at an unsigned-realized position yields an obligation record {site: action/guard_index/src, expr, sort, realization: checked|unchecked|truncated}. An ill-sorted combination yields an obstruction record {site, rule: SORT-affine, core}.
2. Write gen/<M>/sorts/obligations.json.
3. Each obligation feeds the §7.8 realize compilation and the per-site law generator.

items.item: Writer-provenance refinement: same base sort, different writer sets, no value flow gives distinct refined sorts (e.g. queue cursors Idx[queue]_fin = P vs Idx[queue]_inc = T)
items.evidence: P is the state field qpend (Nat, written by finalizeBatch's effect 'qpend'). T is Entry.tot (Nat, written by the commit actions' snoc of Entry with tot = tot+n). Both are plain Nat. There is no writer-set or value-flow analysis: `grep -rn 'provenance|writers|value.flow' holon/` finds nothing.
items.gap: Cursors with the same base sort are not distinguished, so the O16/O33 coherence mismatch cannot surface as a sort conflict.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/sorts/flow.py. Writer sets come from effects per action (field → set of actions; list fields keyed by access path from the index-sensitive analysis). The value-flow graph has edges from each expression's free variables to the target field or let, across lets and def calls.
2. Registers with equal base sort, disjoint writer sets and no flow path between them get distinct sort variables labelled with their writer set.
3. Feed the result to the union-find solver.

items.item: Obligation coherence: a guard κ ⇒ ρ must read a sort written by the action family that ρ constrains
items.evidence: The delay guard in commitBatch and commitBatchWithProof reads `enq_first(qpend, qlen, enq, t)` (def enq_first, morph_rollup.json; L1MessageQueueWithGasPriceOracle.sol:261-268). That is P's sort, while the requirement `n > 0` (reason 5, Rollup.sol:397-399) advances T. The DISCH laws L_disch_delay_* capture the resulting profile semantically, but no code checks coherence.
items.gap: The O16/O33 coherence finding is not produced as a sort/typing error at the guard site.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/sorts/check.py, recognise guards of the shape `rd || !κ || ρ` (or ρ conjoined under κ).
2. Compute Sorts(κ), the sorts κ reads, and Fam(ρ), the actions whose effects advance the sort that ρ constrains.
3. If no sort in Sorts(κ) is written by Fam(ρ), emit a coherence obstruction record {site, kappa_sorts, rho_family, core} into gen/<M>/sorts/obstructions.json. The §7.8 typing step makes it a Bend type error at that site.
4. Add a tests_m2 test asserting the delay-guard site is flagged.

items.item: Untagged unions: detect registers written along edges with distinct refined sorts (σ₁+σ₂); augment with a ghost tag; read at a member sort is an obstruction unless Reach guarantees the member
items.gap: There is no union detection: the union, its tags and its exactness predicate are all hand-authored, and the generator embeds target semantics (version 2 iff tag 2). No check enforces that ghost fields never flow into requires or into non-ghost fields, which the 'adds no behaviour' clause of Prop 6.19 depends on. Exactness is a global invariant over committed entries, not a law per read site ℓ (∀ s ∈ Reach_ℓ. tag(s) = σ).
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/sorts/unions.py. A field whose writer edges carry distinct sorts after solving becomes a union σ₁+σ₂.
2. In holon/gen/machine.py, auto-add a ghost tag companion field per union register; for list or shadow registers, a parallel ghost list. Every writer site assigns the sort id of the value it writes, taken from the assignment, not from hand-written lets.
3. Add a static taint check in machine.py: ghost fields and ghost lets may appear only in ghost lets, ghost effects and observers. Raise FactsError otherwise.
4. Delete the b_tags_exact builtin.
5. For each read site of a union register, generate an exactness law with IR form `∀ p. at_site(p, s0, ℓ) → tag_at_site == σ`, emitted by holon/gen/mlaws.py. Its proof or refutation goes through existing classes plus `counter`.
6. Keep L_tag_BVH as is, since it is frozen in REGISTRY. The generated per-site laws are new law ids.

items.evidence: No union-find or solver anywhere in holon/ (`grep -rni 'union.find|unionfind|union_find'` finds nothing). networkx and z3 are not installed.

items.evidence: There is no cross-component linking. The M0 header facts (Solidity/Go codecs) and the M1 rollup facts (header as hdr_of Nat tokens) are disjoint. Shared constants (249, 257, Z) appear independently: M0 length_by_version; M1 params.Z = 1 with constants_doc. items.item: SORT edge preservation (functoriality of the sort map along every edge)
items.evidence: There are no sorts on carriers or edges (see the §7.1 item). The SORT laws in laws/M1 are only L_sort_remaining (realize) and L_tag_BVH (ghost_tag).
items.gap: Edge preservation is one of the six SORT obligations Thm 6.18 needs, and it is not checked.
items.proposed_work: In holon/sorts/check.py, for each diagram edge, check that the assignment maps the sort of src to the sort of tgt consistently with the edge's declared signature: codec fields keep their sort; STORE then LOAD keeps the register sort; MIG keeps it unless it is a declared migration of sort. A violation is a typing error at the edge site and is recorded in obstructions.json.

items.item: Model generator emits one nominal Bend type per refined sort; affine arithmetic only through typed functions (time_sub, add, realize)
items.evidence: The generated model's types are HEntry/HBD/HCh/HSt/HObs/HAct/Dec_* with Nat fields (gen/M1/model/morph_rollup.bend, e.g. `HSt{t: Nat, lfi: Nat, ..., W: Nat, ...}`). The Bend base has no signed integer: docs/bend_base.txt types are Nat, U32, F32, Bool, Sigma, etc. Record wrappers do work, e.g. `type HBD is Data: HBD{...}`.
items.gap: Sorts are not distinct types, so sort errors cannot become type errors.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/gen/machine.py, read gen/<M>/sorts/assignment.json and emit one wrapper per sort: `type S_Time is Data: S_Time{v: Nat}`, `S_Dur`, `S_IdxFin`, `S_IdxInc`, and so on. Signed sorts become `type S_SDur is Data: SPos{n: Nat} | SNeg{n: Nat}`, or a normalized (a, b) pair.
2. Generate a typed ops library (sort_ops section of the model): time_sub(S_Time, S_Time) -> S_SDur, time_add(S_Time, S_Dur) -> S_Time, idx_add(S_Idx, S_Cnt) -> S_Idx, add_dur_sdur, etc. Generate it only from the §7.2 table.
3. Machine.ex dispatches '+'/'-' on operand sorts; an ill-sorted combination raises FactsError carrying the site.
4. Measure the extra term size against BEND_NOTES §3 (keep each law under about 1,000 fields) before enabling it for the M1 machine.

items.item: Sign obligations become proof arguments: realize(d, proof) at every unsigned realization site, unfillable when an underflow is reachable
items.evidence: laws/M1/L_sort_remaining.json is a hand-written trace law with claim `no_code(obs(p) from s0, 16) == true`. Its meaning depends on the facts having a hand-written require with reason 16 at all three commit actions (morph_rollup.json lines ~1107, ~1499, ~2014). Each of those carries `site: {rule: SORT, kind: realize, expr: 'W + cstart - t'}`, and no code reads it: the only 'site' in holon/ is an unrelated local in mproofs.chain_revert. The outcome is correct (REFUTED at t = s+W+1, replayed as Panic 0x11 at Rollup.sol:363). The `sort_coercion` proof class from docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's M1 plan item 4 is absent from holon/gen/mproofs.py GENERATORS (evaluate, nat_split, noninterference, deadline, chain_revert, counter). Bend 2.0.36 already accepts proof arguments typed as equalities (mproofs core lemmas, e.g. core_kappa_site(..., e: {Bool.and(b, Nat.is_lt(x, t)) == True{} : Bool})).
items.gap: Not every unsigned realization becomes a coercion. Sites with truncated or unchecked subtraction produce no obligation. Removing the require (as mutation MUT2 does at commitBatchWithProof) silently removes the obligation at that site. One law shares reason code 16 across three sites, so a failure is not localized to one site as Thm 6.18 requires.
items.proposed_work:
1. In machine.py, compile every sign-obligation site from gen/<M>/sorts/obligations.json to `realize(d, pf)`, where realize : S_SDur → {is_nonneg(d) == True{} : Bool} → S_Dur.
2. Where a dominating require in the decide chain establishes non-negativity (checked Solidity), the generator threads that branch's equality evidence as pf. Matching on the require's Bool gives it; this is a new helper in the decide-chain builder.
3. Where no dominating guard exists (unchecked or truncated arithmetic), the model keeps a total fallback and the generator emits a per-site coercion-premise law: IR 0.3 `{realize_site: id}` claim `∀ p. at_site(p, s0, id) → nonneg(d_id)`. Write it to laws/<M>/ with one law id per site, never a hole.
4. Add a proof class `coercion_guard` in mproofs.py (the prefix guards imply nonneg, mirroring chain_revert). Refutation reuses the trace explorer plus `counter`.
5. Add tests_m2 checks: every '-' site with a signed result has either a threaded proof or a law, and MUT2 now yields an UNKNOWN/REFUTED per-site law instead of a vanished obligation.

items.item: Writer-provenance becomes typing: delay-guard constructor typed by Idx_inc; passing P (Idx_fin) fails type-checking at that site (O16/O33 coherence)
items.evidence: def enq_first(qpend: Nat, qlen: Nat, enq: List<Nat>, t: Nat) is untyped by cursor sort (morph_rollup.json defs.enq_first). There is no IdxFin/IdxInc type in gen/M1/model/*.bend (`grep '^type' gen/M1` lists only H*/Dec_*/V_* types).
items.gap: The O16/O33 coherence defect cannot appear as a Bend type error at the call site.
items.proposed_work:
1. Once nominal sorts exist, machine.py types def parameters by their assigned sorts.
2. To keep the model executable when the facts are ill-typed, the sort checker (holon/sorts/check.py) detects the mismatch before emission. machine.py then inserts an explicit `reinterpret(x: S_IdxFin, pf: {coherent(site) == True{} : Bool}) -> S_IdxInc` at that site, and the generator emits the coercion premise as a per-site law. That law is unprovable when incoherent, so it ends REFUTED or UNKNOWN and is reported, never silently accepted.
3. Record the site in the result record's `difference` field.

items.item: Unions become ghost-tagged sums: real-code reads compile to as_member(x, tag_proof); the tag proof is the Prop 6.19 law
items.evidence: The ghost tag exists (hand-written, see the §7.4 item), but reads of the union register are plain Nat. In commitBatchWithProof, `let stored = bvh_at(...)`, then `let bvh = ? stored != 0 then stored ...`, which flows straight into the new Entry. No as_member coercion. L_tag_BVH checks a global observer (tags_ok) after the trace, not a per-read coercion premise.
items.gap: Union reads are not coercion sites, so the failure is not localized to the read at Rollup.sol:406/913 (the recommit read).
items.proposed_work:
1. In machine.py, compile each read of a union register at an assumed member sort to `as_member(x, tag, pf: {Nat.is_eq(tag, σ_id) == True{} : Bool})`.
2. As in the realize item, thread pf from a dominating guard where one exists. Otherwise emit the per-read-site exactness law (generated by the §7.4 work) as the coercion premise.
3. Add a proof class `tag_exact` in mproofs.py: reachability induction using the Reach predicate.

Its time candidates are hard-coded deadlines (`new Set([1, s.W, s.W + 1, s.F, s.D + 1])`, plus challenge and enqueue deadlines), and its candidate actions are hand-listed per op.

summary:
Short version: none of the eight §5 rules runs as a rule. Nothing in the code takes a protocol diagram and mechanically derives obligations from it. All 24 laws are IR instances written one at a time. The 8 M0 PAR laws were written by the human and frozen in FROZEN.sha256. The 16 M1 laws were written by the agent; nothing generates them, only readers load them. They are not in FROZEN.sha256: the only lock on them is laws/M1/REGISTRY.json, which the agent wrote itself.

What is genuinely generic and solid:
- The IR to Bend emitters (holon/gen/laws.py, holon/gen/mlaws.py).
- The proof generators that pick a proof by statement shape (open_refl, version_split, noninterference, deadline, chain_revert, nat_split, evaluate, counter).
- The trace refuter that runs on the compiled model (holon/js/explore.mjs).
- Replay on the real code.

The whitepaper defines a diagram 𝔇 (§4.3: carriers, edge kinds, evidence levels, Cm/Cn, symmetry families 𝔉, index-sensitive read/write sets). The code has no diagram data structure:
- holon-facts/0.1 is just typed functions.
- holon-facts/0.2 is a guarded-command machine.
- Evidence levels E1–E6 are hand-typed metadata that is not hashed and that no code reads. Triage comes from a hand-written config/triage.json.

Rule by rule:
- **PAR:** 3 of the 7 sub-forms exist (round trip, cross-component codec, domain coherence), on one carrier (the batch header). Recompute, consumer, branch, initialization and cycle/totality are missing, and there is no path or basis enumeration.
- **UNDO:** both law forms exist, and the noninterference proof generator is generic. Nothing detects undo pairs or computes residues: the residues are built into the model by the hand-written shadow lists in the facts.
- **NAT:** only (a), native equivalence, for η₂ (post hoc). The pre-migration state is a made-up 'legacy' migration, not a version-k machine. (b) naturality and (c) composition are missing.
- **SYM:** one hand-written ω reorder law. No τ/ι/π/μ families, no splits, no promotion logic, no detection of disabling races or sentinels.
- **FACT:** one instance. The collision-freedom premise CF is built into the model abstraction instead of appearing as a premise ∀h. CF(h,S) ⇒ P(h). The freedom-in-bits measure is missing.
- **SORT:** the sign obligation and the ghost tag exist only as observational laws. The facts carry `site` annotations that nothing reads. There is no compilation to typing obligations.
- **DISCH:** blocking is proved for one guard κ, plus 4 profile points whose constants were fixed by hand. The class X is a prefix match on the principal string, not an enableable write closure. There is no Pareto search, no classification into the six classes, no persistent profile and no self-controlled enabledness.
- **OWN:** one alias instance, with ghost fields written by hand. Lost-write is entirely missing.
- **§5.9 intent contracts and §5.10 intent lane:** entirely missing. The frozen schemas also block them: the law schema's rule enum has no INTENT, and the triage enum has no intended_bounded.

The generators also contain Morph-specific code (builtins in machine.py, mcanary LIVE_FIELDS, the deadline shape, eta2 and blobs_of hooks in mreplay). An irrelevant CF premise string is added to every M1 record, including the Go OWN record. All of this has to be removed before the rules can run on a second target in M4.

items.item: Protocol diagram 𝔇 as the data structure every rule reads (carriers, edge kinds, Cm, Cn, 𝔉, Π, index-sensitive R/W sets, interface carriers, sinks, events)
items.evidence: holon/facts.py only knows holon-facts/0.1 typed functions (KIND_TYPES encoder/predicate/decoder/projection). spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json (holon-facts/0.2) has the keys facts_version, target, extraction, abstractions, params, constants_doc, types, state, ghost_state, shadow, initial, principals, reasons, defs, actions, migrations, observers, disch, consumers, coverage. It has no edges, edge kinds, commitments, symmetry families, events or sinks. `grep -rni 'CODEC|edge|carrier|spanning|fundamental|sink' holon` finds only docstrings. Read sets are per field, not per index: holon/gen/machine.py gen_action has `reads = [n for n in state if n in guard_fv]`.
items.gap: §5 says every rule maps 𝔇 to obligations. Def 4.2/4.3 requires kinded edges (CODEC/HASH/STORE/LOAD/CONS/TRANS/MIG/SYM) with component and version labels. TRANS edges carry a principal class, a guard, a cost and index-sensitive read/write sets. 𝔇 also includes M, 𝔉, Cm, Cn and Π. Without this structure no rule can enumerate a basis.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/diagram.py and the schema spec/schemas/diagram.schema.json (holon-diagram/0.1, outside the frozen schemas/).
2. Add holon/gen/diagram.py to build the diagram deterministically from facts:
   - 0.1 functions become CODEC/CONS edges over Header/Bytes/Fields;
   - 0.2 actions become TRANS edges: principal class, guards, cost from disch.cost, reads from the guard free variables, writes from the effects keys, with index sensitivity taken from the win_at/nth/nth_ch/set_ch index arguments;
   - migrations become MIG edges.
3. Extend the facts with optional sections, each with source spans: `commitments`, `interfaces` (R^ext), `symmetry_families`, `events`, `sinks`, and normalised `principal_class` ids.
4. Emit gen/<M>/diagram.json with sorted keys and add it to the G1 byte-identical regeneration.

items.item: Rules as generators: obligations derived mechanically from 𝔇 (holon derive), then frozen before proving
items.evidence: laws/M0/*.json (8) are frozen inputs from the human starter kit. laws/M1/*.json (16) have no producer: `grep -rn 'laws/M1' holon tools` finds only readers (holon/ir.py:60, holon/mreplay.py:300, tests_m1/test_m1_results.py:24). holon/gen/laws.py and holon/gen/mlaws.py are IR→LAWS.bend emitters, not rule generators. Every M1 law hard-codes its instance: L_undo_BVH names revertBatch{who:1,count:1}; L_sym_omega names is_commitBatchWithProof/is_challengeState; L_disch_delay_* embed the s* trace and the constants cost=1 and elapsed=0/19.
items.gap: App. E gives each rule a basis: fundamental cycles plus evidenced pairs (PAR), pair × residue (UNDO), entry points × in-flight types (NAT), generators (SYM), commitment × consumer (FACT), edges (SORT), guard conjuncts (DISCH), views × writers (OWN). Nothing enumerates any of these. Coverage is therefore whatever someone thought to write, completeness relative to 𝔇 (Thm 6.4, 6.7c, Prop 6.11) cannot be claimed, and the M3 blind rerun is impossible.
items.proposed_work:
1. Create holon/rules/__init__.py: a registry mapping each rule to derive(diagram, facts) → [law IR holon-ir/0.3], plus a provenance entry per law (rule, subform, basis element, evidence, source nodes/spans).
2. Add `python -m holon derive --milestone M3 --out laws/M3/`. It writes the IR, REGISTRY.json and DERIVATION.json in sorted order. law_id is a deterministic function of rule, subform and basis element.
3. Add tests_m3/test_derive.py: the derive output must equal the frozen laws/M3 byte for byte (no hand edits, no cherry-picking).
4. The human freezes laws/M3 into FROZEN.sha256 before any `holon run`.
5. Back-test: derive over facts/morph_header.json should reproduce the 8 M0 statements, and over the spec/M1 facts the 16 M1 shapes. Report any differences as Surprises.

items.item: Evidence levels E1–E6 computed from 𝔇 and used to gate obligations (strong/medium → defect; weak E6 → intent question)
items.evidence: `evidence` is a hand-typed array in each law IR. holon/ir.py HASHED_KEYS excludes it ('notes and evidence are metadata'), and `grep -rni evidence holon` finds no consumer. Triage comes from the hand-written config/triage.json (e.g. L_par_hdr_ssvh → intent_question), read by holon/pipeline.py:46 and holon/mpipeline.py:203.
items.gap: PAR obligations need evidence of at least medium level (§5.1). Weak evidence must produce intent questions, not defects (§4.5). SYM promotion (§5.4(i)) depends on E1–E4. None of this is computed.

items.item: M1 obligations are frozen by agent-written hashes, not by the human
items.evidence: FROZEN.sha256 covers laws/M0 (9 entries) but has 0 entries for laws/M1 or spec/M1 (`grep -c 'laws/M1\|spec/M1' FROZEN.sha256` → 0). The session that wrote the proofs also wrote laws/M1/REGISTRY.json. spec/M1/predictions.json was transcribed by the agent. Its L_tag_BVH row adds '(either direction of the version swap is the same obstruction O26)' after the search found v1→v2, whereas §11.8 says 'commit v2; revert; commitState v1' (docs/M1_REPORT.md §2.5). Two laws were added post hoc: L_disch_delay_prove and L_nat_eta2.
items.gap: §5: obligations 'are compiled into frozen laws'. §9.4 requires statements to be frozen before proving. For M1, gate G2 only checks hashes the agent wrote.
items.proposed_work:
1. Under 'Questions for the human', ask the human to freeze laws/M1/*.json and spec/M1/predictions.json (tools/freeze.py write is human-only).

items.item: Morph-specific shortcuts inside the generic generators, canaries, replay and records
items.evidence:
- holon/gen/machine.py Machine.builtin hard-codes win_at, win_last, nth_ch, set_ch, any_open, clear_chs, zero_csr, set_last_csr, tags_exact, hdr_of, bump_f, agg(AGG_BASE), es_<shadow>, go_append_heap/go_append_slice/go_read. gen_record_lib emits b_bump_go, b_any_open and b_tags_exact keyed on the Entry and Ch types.
- holon/mcanary.py has LIVE_FIELDS=[s_bvh,s_tag,t,paused,inch,qlen].
- holon/gen/mproofs.py _kappa_shape requires `b && x + get(nth_ch(chs,i),f) < t`.
- holon/mreplay.py:127 has `if t['mig']=='eta2'` and linearises claims by the names blobs_of/new_hdr/no_code.
- holon/mpipeline.py:233 appends 'CF(keccak256, headers)…' to every record, including results/M1/L_own_txspayload.json (a Go heap machine with no keccak).
items.gap: Rules must run on any diagram, including the M4 held-out target. Today the trusted-path generators carry target-specific code, and records list premises that do not apply to them.
items.proposed_work:
1. Move the Morph helpers into facts `defs` written in the DSL, or into spec/<target>/lib.json compiled by machine.py. Keep only generic List/Nat builtins in holon/gen/machine.py.
2. Derive the erase_live canary fields from Machine.reads instead of LIVE_FIELDS.
3. Generalise `deadline` to κ = b ∧ deadline(s) < t, with frame lemmas derived from the effects.
4. Make mreplay dispatch on IR shape (generic migration chains) and take its replay hooks from the facts.
5. Take record premises from a per-facts `premises` section, not a hard-coded string.

items.item: No schema for holon-ir/0.2 (or a future 0.3), which derived laws need
items.evidence: The frozen schemas/law_ir.schema.json requires statement.forall with binder types in {Header, Bytes}, so it describes only holon-ir/0.1. The M1 laws use `binders` (State/Trace/Act/Nat/Bool), `exists`, `all`, `proj`, `obs`, `mig`. No schema validates them. holon/ir.py IR_VERSIONS=('holon-ir/0.1','holon-ir/0.2').
items.gap: Derived obligations need a validated IR. The schemas/ directory is frozen.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add spec/schemas/law_ir_0_3.schema.json covering binders, exists, conjunctions, proj, obs, mig, CF premises and the INTENT rule.
2. Validate laws in tests_m3 using the installed jsonschema 4.26.
3. Ask the human whether it should move under the frozen schemas/.

items.item: PAR rule generator: parallel-path enumeration, fundamental-cycle basis for the invertible fragment, evidenced pairs for the lossy fragment, PAR-cycle (O7)
items.evidence: No path or cycle enumeration anywhere (`grep -rn 'spanning|fundamental|cycle' holon` returns nothing). The 8 PAR laws are the frozen hand-written laws/M0. laws/M1 has no PAR law. O7 (lastBlockNumber cycle) and O3 (router domain) have no law.
items.gap: Thm 6.4 and Cor 6.5 call for |E|−|V|+κ fundamental-cycle checks over a spanning tree. Prop 6.11 says lossy obligations are enumerated from evidenced pairs. HASH edges count as invertible only under explicit CF premises (Cor 6.16).
items.proposed_work:
Add holon/rules/par.py:
1. Build the invertible fragment from diagram edges. Injectivity comes from layout-inverse encoders; HASH edges are invertible only under an explicit CF premise.
2. Build a deterministic spanning tree (sorted BFS) and emit one holonomy law per non-tree edge.
3. Emit one law per lossy pair with evidence of E5 or better.
4. Pick the subform tag from the edge kinds.
5. Reuse holon/gen/proofs.py (open_refl, version_split) and holon/refute.py.
6. Derive pins from encoder domain and version guards and from layout-algebra constant cells (e.g. enc_sol's constant ssvh cell), so that derive over facts/morph_header.json reproduces L_par_hdr_v0/v1/v2, L_rt_go_v0..2 and L_dom_hdr.

items.item: PAR sub-form: round trip
items.evidence: laws/M0/L_rt_go_v0/v1/v2.json (subform round_trip; frozen, hand-written) are PROVED by holon/gen/proofs.py open_refl and checked by BendTT (results/M0/L_rt_go_v*.json).
items.gap: Covers only Go dec ∘ Solidity enc for the header, written by hand. No round trips for the block-context codec (D3), the blob/compression pipeline or ParseBatch.
items.proposed_work: Have rules/par.py emit a round-trip law for every (encoder, decoder) pair on a carrier with E1 evidence. Extend the facts (M2 extraction) to block contexts and the blob codec, so new laws need no new code.

items.item: PAR sub-form: cross-component codec agreement
items.evidence: laws/M0/L_par_hdr_v0/v1/v2/ssvh.json: v0 and v1 PROVED; v2 and ssvh REFUTED (results/M0), with v2 replayed on Go.
items.gap: Header only, and written by hand. There is no derivation of per-version laws from encoder domain guards.
items.proposed_work: Generate these from rules/par.py: one law per version in the encoder domain (enc_sol domain.version_le, Go encoder lengths), with the premises pinned by holon/gen/laws.py collect_pins.

items.item: PAR sub-form: recomputation (E4), e.g. O6 legacy Go data hash vs the on-chain formula
items.evidence: No law has a recompute subform. facts/morph_header.json has no data-hash functions. spec/M1/facts/morph_batchdata.json coverage.debt lists DataHash and DataHashV2.
items.gap: An obligation for each value that one path stores and another path recomputes.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add facts for DataHash_sol and DataHashV2_go as edges into Dig[data] (an M2 extraction target).
2. Have rules/par.py emit a recompute law wherever a STORE write and a recompute over the same inputs coexist (E4).
3. Refute through holon/refute.py.

items.item: PAR sub-form: consumer agreement (O8: trailing payload ignored by derivation; circuit is an oracle)
items.evidence: The facts' `consumers` holds only blobs_of, which FACT uses. The derivation pipeline (Stream→Parse→Derived) and the circuit oracle are not in any facts file. No PAR consumer law exists.
items.gap: An agreement obligation between consumers that read the same committed carrier, split on oracle hypotheses (HypC).
items.proposed_work:
1. Add facts for Go ParseBatch and for the circuit as a hypothesis predicate.
2. Have rules/par.py emit pairwise consumer laws per committed carrier, with the oracle hypothesis as an explicit premise.
items.depends_on: PAR rule generator; Cm/Cn in diagram

items.item: PAR sub-form: branch agreement (O5: the estimator's fast path vs its slow path)
items.evidence: No branch subform exists. EstimateCompressedSizeWithNewPayload is in morph_batchdata coverage.debt.
items.gap: Path equality between alternative internal branches, including definedness.
items.proposed_work:
1. Let the facts DSL declare alternative branches as parallel edges with the same source and target.
2. Have rules/par.py emit a branch-equality law for each pair.
3. Refute with holon/js/explore.mjs or holon/refute.py.

items.item: PAR sub-form: initialization coherence (E3 equations hold in initial states; O9 genesis cursor; D4 invariant)
items.evidence: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json `initial` is a hand-written post-genesis state, and coverage.debt lists importGenesisBatch and initialize. No law is stated at initializers. docs/M1_REPORT.md §7 says D4 needs Reach induction and was not done.
items.gap: E3 equations must hold after every initializer, and the invariants must be inductive over Reach.
items.proposed_work:
1. Model the initializers as TRANS edges from an uninitialized state.
2. Have rules/par.py emit a law that each E3 guard equation holds after every initializer.
3. Add a Reach-based `invariant` proof generator in holon/gen/mproofs.py (step preservation, generalised from `deadline`) for D4-style invariants.

items.item: PAR domain coherence at every interface carrier on R^ext (O1 done; O3 router domain missing)
items.evidence: laws/M0/L_dom_hdr.json (ok_sol b == ok_go b over all Bytes) is REFUTED with 250 zero bytes (results/M0/L_dom_hdr.json) and replayed through the real Rollup._loadBatchHeader. The facts do not mark interface carriers or R^ext, so there is one law for one carrier.
items.gap: The rule must enumerate every decoder at every interface carrier, pairwise, over R^ext.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add a facts section `interfaces: {carrier: {decoders, ext}}`.
2. Have rules/par.py emit pairwise ok_i == ok_j laws per interface carrier.
3. Add the verifier-router domain predicate to the facts for O3.

items.item: PAR 'including definedness' and PAR-totality (O4: clone panics on non-canonical elements)
items.evidence: In M0, definedness is explicit: holon/facts.py UNDEF=0xDEAD, and holon/refute.py requires every subterm to be defined. The M1 machine models reverts as O_Rev observations. No totality law exists, and O4 is not modelled.
items.gap: A definedness conjunct for every partial edge pair, and panic sites treated as partial domains.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/par.py add a def(p x) == def(q x) obligation whenever either side is partial (a decoder guard, or a panic site recorded in the facts).
2. Extract Go panic sites in M2.

items.item: UNDO pair detection (ā's guard reads a's writes; ā restores a cursor a advanced; ā emits an inverse event)
items.evidence: The pairs (commitBatch, revertBatch) and (challengeState, setPause(true)) are written by hand into laws/M1/L_undo_BVH.json and L_undo_cancel.json. The facts have no events (`grep -n 'events\|emit' spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json` → none). Machine.reads (holon/gen/machine.py gen_action) computes guard read sets, but nothing intersects them with write sets.
items.gap: All three detection criteria are unimplemented.

items.item: UNDO residue computation Res(a,ā)(s) = {r : (ā∘a)(s)(r) ≠ s(r)}
items.evidence: The facts author put the residues into the model by hand as shadow lists (morph_rollup.json `shadow`: s_csr, s_bd, s_bvh, s_tag; abstractions[3]). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4 says the window/shadow representation 'makes UNDO non-interference structural'. No code computes residues.
items.gap: Residues must be computed from the model, not chosen through the representation.
items.proposed_work:
1. In rules/undo.py, compute Res statically: fields and indices written by a and not restored by ā (effects diff plus index analysis).
2. Confirm it dynamically: holon/js/machine.mjs evaluates run([a,ā], s) against s over the explorer's corpus of reachable states.
3. Generate the window/shadow split in holon/gen/machine.py from the computed residue (per-index map → window+shadow) instead of hand-writing it.
4. Emit one dead_residue law per residue register.

items.item: UNDO dead-residue obligation (bisimulation 'equal outside Res')
items.evidence: laws/M1/L_undo_CSR.json and L_undo_BD.json (subform dead_residue: proj-erasure non-interference from any two states over all traces) are PROVED by holon/gen/mproofs.py noninterference, which is generic and picked by shape. The 12 erase_live canaries in holon/mcanary.py are rejected. Mutation 4 in spec/M1/mutations.json flips L_undo_CSR.
items.gap: The proof route is fine, but the erased field is chosen by hand. The residue liveness distance (Def 6.13) is not reported.
items.proposed_work:
1. Feed the residue output of rules/undo.py into dead_residue law emission.
2. Record the liveness distance in REFUTED records: the BFS depth of the first observation that depends on the residue, from explore.mjs divergence().

items.item: UNDO live residue: undo-pair law refuted by a trace
items.evidence: L_undo_BVH and L_undo_cancel are REFUTED, with witnesses from holon/js/explore.mjs divergence search, and replayed on the real Rollup through holon/mreplay.py (results/M1, replay/M1/report.json).
items.gap: The instances are chosen by hand. 'Cancel' is modelled as setPause(true) by hand.
items.proposed_work: Generate these laws from the detected pairs in rules/undo.py. Keep the existing refuter and counter generator.

items.item: Versioned machines S_k, A_k and MIG edges (the prerequisite for NAT)
items.evidence: There is one machine per facts file (holon/gen/machine.py). The facts' migrations are just `legacy` (zeroes the CSR of a new-version state) and `eta2`. coverage.debt lists initialize3 and initialize4. There are no version-k actions.
items.gap: NAT(b) needs op^k. Old-version reachable states are approximated, without any check, as new-version states with CSR zeroed.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add a facts section `versions: {k: {state_delta, action_overrides}}` and typed MIG k→k+1 edges.
2. machine.py emits step_k and run_k per version, sharing the unchanged actions.
3. Legacy states then come from run_k(p, s0_k), not from a pseudo-migration.
4. Write the facts per version by hand until M2 extracts them from the upgrade commits.

items.item: NAT native equivalence op^{k+1}(η(s)) ≈ op^{k+1}(s^nat)
items.evidence: laws/M1/L_nat_eta2.json (post hoc) compares obs(q) from eta2(legacy(run p s0), csr_last) with obs(q) from run p s0. It is REFUTED and replayed by emulating the pre-v2 storage (holon/mreplay.py:127 special-cases mig 'eta2').
items.gap: One migration out of η₂, η₃, η₄, η_enq, η_BVH and the cutover. In-flight object types and new-version entry points are not enumerated (Thm 6.7c). The O13, O14, O16 and O17 instances are absent.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/rules/nat.py: for each MIG edge × each in-flight type (registers indexed by objects in flight at migration, from the diagram) × each new-version entry point that reads it, emit a native-equivalence law.
2. Add facts for η_enq, η_BVH, η₃/η₄ and the submitter-registry cutover.

items.item: NAT naturality η ∘ op^k = op^{k+1} ∘ η
items.evidence: No law has a naturality subform. It cannot be stated without op^k, since there is no versioned machine.
items.gap: A naturality square per entry point that exists in both versions.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/nat.py emit the squares.
2. Add a generator `naturality_step` to holon/gen/mproofs.py, modelled on noninterference: generalise over the decision, close each branch.
3. Refute with explore.mjs.

items.item: NAT composition coherence across reachable migration sequences (O18: η₄ before η₃ leaves D = 0)
items.evidence: No law exists, and there are no η₃/η₄ facts (coverage.debt lists initialize3 and initialize4).
items.gap: All reachable migration orders must coincide.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/nat.py enumerate the migration orders the reinitializer guards allow.
2. Emit an equality of continuations for each pair of orders.
3. Search the orders with explore.mjs.

items.item: SYM candidate families τ (time), ι (index), π (principal within role), μ (unit scaling) as generated state and input transforms
items.evidence: No transform exists. The only `perm` (holon/gen/machine.py:729) is the permissionless-action predicate, not a permutation. Only ω exists, through one hand-written law.
items.gap: Families must be admitted by sorts and applied as group or monoid actions on states and inputs.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/rules/sym.py and a facts or diagram section `symmetry_families` derived from the sort assignment (§7.7).
2. machine.py generates tau(s,δ), tau_act(a,δ), iota, pi and mu from register and input sorts.

items.item: SYM per-action equivariance and split reporting A = A_eq ⊎ A_break
items.evidence: No equivariance law, split computation or split report exists.
items.gap: Equivariance must be checked per generator and per action, and the split reported rather than promoted by frequency.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/sym.py emit, per generator g and action a, step(g·a, g·s) == g·step(a, s) together with observation equivariance.
2. Add holon/sym_split.py to aggregate the outcomes into results/<M>/sym_splits.json.

items.item: SYM split promotion: only via strong evidence, an intent contract or the intent lane, or auditor two-hypothesis adjudication
items.evidence: No promotion logic exists. Findings are triaged only through config/triage.json.
items.gap: The whitepaper explicitly forbids promoting a split by frequency (the v1 behaviour).

items.item: SYM reordering pairs ω (different principal classes, both orders execute, results differ on a sink-reaching register)
items.evidence: laws/M1/L_sym_omega.json has premises runs_ok([a,b]) and runs_ok([b,a]). It is REFUTED and replayed (O19). The principal-class difference (anyone vs challenger) was chosen by hand. The claim compares every observation of a continuation, not sink-reaching registers. No pairs are enumerated.
items.gap: Pairs must be enumerated and filtered by principal class and by sink reachability.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/sym.py enumerate action pairs with different normalised principal classes.
2. Emit a reorder law with premises that both orders execute.
3. Restrict the claim to the registers that reach a sink (diagram `sinks`), using the existing proj/View machinery in holon/gen/mlaws.py.

items.item: SYM: disabling races classified separately
items.evidence: Nothing classifies them. The ω law simply assumes that both orders execute.
items.gap: Pairs where only one order executes need their own class.
items.proposed_work: Have rules/sym.py emit a runs_ok([a,b]) == runs_ok([b,a]) law with subform disabling_race, triaged separately in results.

items.item: SYM sentinels: constants compared against Time- or Idx-sorted registers (O21 `enq = 0`; D6 harmless sentinels)
items.evidence: No sentinel scan exists, and registers carry no sorts (all values are Nat: abstractions[0]).
items.gap: Translation splits should localise sentinel conflation.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/sym.py scan facts guards for comparisons of Time- or Idx-sorted terms with constants.
2. Emit τ/ι equivariance laws restricted to the actions that read them.
3. Report D6-style discharges as PROVED.

items.item: FACT rule generator over commitments × consumers in scope
items.evidence: laws/M1/L_fact_Z.json was written by hand. The facts have `consumers: {blobs_of}` only and no `commitments`. The commitment is the hand-written observer new_hdr.
items.gap: Kernel containment for every commitment m and every consumer c in its scope. The O23, O24 and O25 instances are absent.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add a facts section `commitments` (header hash, versioned hash, data hash, public input), each giving the carrier it commits.
2. Have rules/fact.py emit ker(m) ⊆ ker(c) laws in the L_fact_Z two-run shape for each (m, c).

items.item: FACT collision-freedom as explicit local premises ∀h. CF(h,S) ⇒ P(h)
items.evidence: CF is built into the model rather than stated. morph_rollup.json abstractions say committedBatches is not stored, header equality stands for hash equality, and agg() is an injective stand-in for keccak. holon/mpipeline.py:233 adds a CF string to the record premises. The hashed statements contain no CF premise.
items.gap: An injective stand-in proves P(agg), not ∀h. CF(h,S) ⇒ P(h). The premise is not part of the hashed claim.
items.proposed_work:
1. IR 0.3: add an abstract `Hash` function binder and a premise form cf(h, S) over the statement's own terms. The emitter generates the hypothesis binders h x == h y → x == y.
2. machine.py takes h as a parameter instead of agg.
3. Counter-laws instantiate h with the injective stand-in (consistent per Thm 6.15).

items.item: FACT quantitative form: adversarial freedom F(m,c) in bits
items.evidence: `grep -rni 'freedom|bits|log2' holon` finds nothing.
items.gap: FACT should report the adversary's freedom in bits.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/rules/fact_freedom.py with a collection mode in explore.mjs that gathers the distinct consumer values reachable with equal commitments within the bound.
2. Record freedom_bits_lower_bound together with the bound in REFUTED FACT records.

items.item: FACT proof route for PROVED instances (product program)
items.evidence: The only FACT law is REFUTED. holon/gen/mproofs.py GENERATORS has no two-run product generator.
items.gap: Kernel containment cannot be certified true today.
items.proposed_work: Add an mproofs `product` generator for the two-run shape: induct on the shared prefix, generalise over the decisions, and show that the consumer is a function of the committed fields under the CF hypotheses.

items.item: SORT sign obligations (realize sites)
items.evidence: laws/M1/L_sort_remaining.json claims no_code(obs p, 16), i.e. no Panic 0x11, and is REFUTED. The underflow is modelled as a facts guard with reason 16 and a `site` annotation ({rule: SORT, kind: realize}, 3 copies in morph_rollup.json). No generator consumes it: grep 'site' in holon finds only a local variable in mproofs.chain_revert.
items.gap: In v2, sorts compile to Bend types, and each realize site becomes a coercion premise. Obligations are generated per site, not written as one hand law.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/sort.py enumerate every `site`, and every checked subtraction on uint-realized terms, and emit a per-site law now.
2. Migrate them to coercion premises once §7.8 typed models exist.

items.item: SORT: no untagged-union reads at a member sort (ghost-tag exactness)
items.evidence: laws/M1/L_tag_BVH.json (the tags_ok observer) is REFUTED. The ghost field s_tag/tag is hand-written in the facts, and tags_exact is a hard-coded Morph builtin in machine.py. It checks a window-wide invariant, not read-site exactness ∀s ∈ Reach_ℓ. tag(s) = σ.
items.gap: Ghost tags should be generated per union register, with one law per read site.
items.proposed_work:
1. Infer union-typed registers from sorts.
2. machine.py adds generated ghost tag fields, written by each writer.
3. rules/sort.py emits a law per (site ℓ, member σ) over the pre-state of each successful step that reaches ℓ.

items.item: SORT: edge preservation, width (O28 uint16), conservation (O30/D8), payer/bearer keying (O29)
items.evidence: No laws exist. Values are unbounded Nat (abstractions[0]), with no ABI widths. Accounting and the messenger replay budget are in coverage.debt.
items.gap: Four of the six sort obligation kinds have no law form at all.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add ABI widths to the facts.
2. rules/sort.py emits width laws at realize-in-width sites.
3. Model value flows and emit conservation laws.
4. Add messenger and replay facts for payer/bearer keying.

items.item: DISCH: enumerate guard conjuncts κ ⇒ ρ with the obligated class X
items.evidence: κ is a hand-written observer `kappa` in the facts. The delay guard and the state s* were chosen by hand, and the laws embed the s* trace.
items.gap: Obligations must come from every guard conjunct.
items.proposed_work: Have rules/disch.py split each facts `require` into conjuncts, recognise the κ ⇒ ρ form (['||', ['!', κ], ρ]), take X from the action's principal class, and emit observers and laws mechanically.

items.item: DISCH enableable write closure Write*_X (writer callable by X, guard makeable true by X's actions and time)
items.evidence: holon/gen/machine.py:729 defines perm(a) as the actions whose free-text principal starts with 'anyone' or 'environment'. There is no fixpoint and no enablement analysis.
items.gap: This is exactly the v1 omission that v2 fixes: permissionless writers guarded by another principal's state must not count for X.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/disch.py compute Write*_X as a least fixpoint over TRANS edges. An action is kept only if each guard conjunct's reads lie in Write*_X ∪ {t} ∪ inputs, or if a bounded X-strategy search makes it hold.
2. Emit a generated x_closure(a) predicate into the model in place of perm.
3. Record the closure in DERIVATION.json.
4. Normalise principals into class ids.

items.item: DISCH blocking invariant
items.evidence:
- L_disch_stale (κ preserved by every perm action and by time, from any state) is PROVED by mproofs.deadline.
- L_disch_stale_commit (κ ⇒ commitBatchWithProof reverts) is PROVED by mproofs.chain_revert.
- The deadline generator is shape-specific (_kappa_shape).
- The Read(κ) ∩ Write*_X = ∅ condition is not computed; the invariant is proved directly, which is a sound substitute.
- No law shows that a named class Y can discharge, so 'external-dependent' is only half certified.
items.gap: The closure is not used, the generator is narrow, and there is no exists-strategy law for X ∪ Y.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have rules/disch.py emit preservation laws over x_closure, per-action revert laws, and an exists-strategy law for X ∪ Y.
2. Generalise `deadline` into an invariant_frame generator driven by the computed read/write sets.

items.item: DISCH discharge profile DP_X: a Pareto set computed by bi-criteria label-correcting search, each point a strategy law
items.evidence:
- holon/js/explore.mjs strategies() runs a plain BFS for a witness to a hand-written exists law whose cost and elapsed constants are fixed in the law.
- There is no finite abstraction and there are no cost × delay labels or Pareto set.
- L_disch_delay_nofree proves only that one commitBatch from s* fails for every n.
- Nothing certifies that {(1,0), (0,19), (1000,0)} is Pareto-minimal.
- L_disch_delay_prove was added post hoc.
- s* was chosen by hand (docs/M1_REPORT.md §5).
items.gap: Profiles must be computed, not asserted point by point, and minimality must be evidenced.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/rules/disch_profile.py: a deterministic finite abstraction over the guard-relevant registers, edges labelled from facts disch.cost and wait dt, and label-correcting search.
2. Emit the profile_point exists laws from the search output, never with hand-written constants.
3. Emit bounded dominance laws, e.g. ∀ strategies with |st| ≤ H and cost < c ⇒ elapsed ≥ δ, with scope bounded(H).
4. Derive s* per guard class from the explorer.

items.item: DISCH profile classification: Immediate / Cost-bearing / Delay-dischargeable / Mixed / External-dependent / Non-dischargeable
items.evidence: No classifier exists. 'Mixed' for O33 is asserted only in the docs. O32 (the BVH pin, non-dischargeable) has no DISCH law, only the UNDO refutation. O34 (the replay budget, external: owner) is unmodelled because the messenger is not in the facts.
items.gap: Classification from DP_X and DP_{X∪Y}. Non-dischargeable needs a law that every principal is blocked.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/rules/disch_classify.py to classify from the computed profiles.
2. Emit an all-principals blocking invariant for the non-dischargeable class.
3. Record the class in result records (a new schema outside the frozen schemas/, or ask the human).
4. Add messenger facts for O34.

items.item: DISCH persistent profile (strategies that keep κ false until its next trigger)
items.evidence: No persistent mode exists in explore.mjs or in the laws.

summary:
An honest map of the theory layer (whitepaper §6, §10.3, §10.6–10.7) against the M1 code. What exists is instance-level machinery. None of the framework-level mechanisms the whitepaper describes are in the code.

What is real and kernel-checked:
(1) The Thm 6.9(i) deadness certificate. holon/gen/mproofs.py noninterference() builds per-action step lemmas over the decide/exec split, then inducts on the trace. L_undo_CSR and L_undo_BD are PROVED, unbounded, and dual-kernel, and the erase_live canaries are rejected.
(2) A Thm 6.10 blocking invariant, but only for one hard-coded guard shape: deadline() plus chain_revert() for L_disch_stale and L_disch_stale_commit.
(3) Discharge-profile points as concrete straight-line strategies, checked by evaluation. L_disch_delay_pay, _wait and _prove start from one hand-picked state s*, and their cost and delay constants are written into hand-authored law IR.
(4) Thm 6.9(ii) refutations by the divergence BFS in holon/js/explore.mjs, replayed on Foundry.
(5) A ghost-tag law (L_tag_BVH), REFUTED.

What is missing or diverged:
- **Core library.** It is not formalized once. The CORE in mproofs.py is ten Nat/Bool lemmas held as a Python string and pasted into 2 of 16 proof files. None of Thm 6.4, 6.6, 6.7, Lemma 6.2, Thm 6.3, Cor 6.5 or Lemma 6.12 is formalized. A grep for spanning|fundamental|holonomy|equivarian|natural|pasting finds nothing.
- **Basis reduction (§10.3).** No step exists as code. There is no diagram graph, no invertible-fragment classification, no spanning tree or fundamental cycles, no SYM generators, and no NAT entry-point enumeration. Every law in laws/M0 and laws/M1 is hand-written IR.
- **CF(h,S) premises.** Diverged. IR 0.2 has no function-typed binder, so ∀h. CF(h,S) → P(h) cannot be written. Instead:
  - hashes are abstracted away (a header is presented by its index; committedBatches is "k ≤ LCI");
  - keccak over blob hashes is replaced by one concrete injective function (agg, built from Cantor pairing);
  - a CF premise string is attached to every M1 record, including the Go OWN law, which involves no hashing.
  The checker itself supports the right form (bend/probes/p12_fn_premise.bend).
- **Prop 6.21.** There is no bi-criteria label-correcting search. strategies() in explore.mjs is a BFS that returns the first trace matching constants already pinned in the law. No code computes a Pareto set, proves minimality, computes the persistent variant or classifies a profile, and there is no finite abstraction beyond a hand-written Morph policy in policy_lib.mjs.
- **Static deadness analysis (§10.6).** Missing. Key-sensitivity comes from hand-declared shadow lists in the facts, validated only by replay.
- **Ghost tags (Prop 6.19).** Only half there. The "augmentation adds no behaviour" condition is never checked: Machine.ghost_state is loaded and unused, and decide_commitState and decide_commitBatchWithProof take +s_tag as a parameter. The PROVED direction is impossible because there is no Reach induction (planned for M1 in ARCHITECTURE.md, not delivered).
- **Other gaps:**
  - There are no Def 6.13 quantitative measures and no F(m,c).
  - There is no "split" status.
  - Counter-laws of exists or conjunctive laws are unsupported, so a false profile point can never be REFUTED.
  - Thm 6.18 (sorts as types) diverged: SORT is modelled as reverting requires plus a reachability law.
- **Not ready for per-target instantiation (M4).** The "generic" generators contain Morph-specific code: machine.py builtins (nth_ch, bump_f, tags_exact), deadline()'s hard-coded "Ch" record, mcanary.LIVE_FIELDS, and policy_lib.mjs.

**Questions for the human:**
- CSR_i is readable through the public getter committedStateRoots(i), but observations in the model are only revert codes. Should view getters count as observations in Thm 6.9? The PROVED status of L_undo_CSR depends on the answer.
- laws/M1 and spec/M1 are not listed in FROZEN.sha256. They are protected only by REGISTRY.json (gate check G2), and the registry is not frozen either. The proposed basis-reduction step would generate new obligations, so it needs a human freeze path.
