A grep for 'slither|go/ssa|golang.org/x/tools|\byul\b|ast-compact|--ast|--ir|solcx|frontend' over holon/ tools/ tests/ tests_m1/ spec/ config/ returns nothing. facts/morph_header.json extraction.method is 'hand-written from the audit bundle'; spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json extraction.method is 'hand-written from the real repo at the pinned commit (M1)'. Verified in the container: /root/work/solc-0.8.24 --evm-version cancun --ast-compact-json on contracts/l1/rollup/Rollup.sol, run in /root/work/holon-replay-m1/solidity with remappings to node_modules, produces 12 AST files. Rollup has 42 FunctionDefinitions, 3 ModifierDefinitions, 8 InlineAssembly nodes and 31 YulFunctionCalls; BatchHeaderCodecV0 has 24 InlineAssembly nodes. --ir produces Rollup.yul with 311 mstore occurrences. --storage-layout works. /root/work/morph/contracts has no node_modules, so the deps come from the replay workspace or replay.py:_sol_deps. Slither is not installed (pip dry-run: slither-analyzer 0.11.6 installable).
items.gap: The whitepaper wants facts produced from the solc AST, Yul and Slither IR. Today every Solidity fact is transcribed by hand, and nothing reads compiler output.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/solidity/compile.py. It runs the pinned solc (path in config/holon.json) with --evm-version taken from foundry.toml, remappings from remappings.txt, and deps installed through the existing replay._sol_deps. It writes build/extract/<sha>/ast/*.json, *.yul and storage.json, with no timestamps, and records the solc version and the sha256 of every input source.
2. Add holon/frontends/solidity/ast.py: a deterministic walker, sorted by src offset, that also parses InlineAssembly Yul ASTs and resolves externalReferences.
3. Optionally add slither_ir.py, behind a pinned slither-analyzer==0.11.6 installed by a new `tools/setup_env.sh --extract`. Use its SlithIR for the modifier/require CFG and read/write sets.
4. Output a new holon-facts/0.3 file, spec/M2/facts/<target>.extracted.json. This is a generated file, so G1 must regenerate it; it never overwrites the frozen facts/.
5. Add tests_m2/test_extract_solidity.py: running the extraction twice gives byte-identical output.

items.item: Storage families -> state carriers
items.evidence: The state in spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json ('state', 'shadow', 'ghost_state') is hand-written. It uses a manual window/shadow abstraction (abstractions[3]: per-batch registers in window LFI..LCI plus shadow lists). committedBatches is not stored at all (abstractions[2]). solc --storage-layout gives the real families (slots 151-174: committedBatches, batchDataStore struct, challenges struct, committedStateRoots, batchBlobVersionedHashes, ...), but no code consumes it.
items.gap: State carriers should be generated from storage families: mappings keyed by index, with structs flattened into register families. Here they are chosen and abstracted by hand.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/solidity/storage.py. It maps the storageLayout JSON to holon-facts state entries: a mapping(uint256=>T) becomes an index-keyed family; struct members become sub-registers; elementary types carry their width; __gap entries are skipped. Each entry gets a src span from astId.
2. Emit an 'abstraction' section that names any window/shadow representation as an explicit derived view. The model generator (holon/gen/machine.py) then compiles either the raw families or the windowed view.
3. Add tests_m2: compare the extracted families with the register set of the hand-written M1 facts (CB, CSR, BVH, BD, CH, LCI, LFI, ...) and report differences as coverage debt, never as silent drops.

items.item: External functions -> TRANS edges with guards from require and modifiers, index-sensitive read/write sets, principal class
items.evidence: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json actions[*].guards are hand-transcribed require lists with src lines; for example commitBatch has 'require mem who active' for the onlyActiveSubmitter modifier at Rollup.sol:120 and the whenNotPaused require from PausableUpgradeable.sol:77. Principals are free text ('active submitter'). Rollup.sol has 70 require( calls and 3 modifiers (onlyActiveSubmitter, onlyChallenger, nonReqRevert). holon/gen/machine.py computes read sets from the hand-written guards (Machine.reads), not from code.
items.gap: Guards, effects, read/write sets and principal classes should be extracted from public/external functions with their modifiers inlined. None of this is automated.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/solidity/transitions.py. For each external/public non-view function: inline the modifiers; walk the statements in order; turn require/if-revert into a guard {require, reason, src}; turn straight-line storage assignments into effects; take reads and writes from the AST or SlithIR, keyed by index expression.
2. Classify the principal from the msg.sender checks in modifiers: onlyOwner gives owner, onlyActiveSubmitter gives an oracle-checked role.
3. Emit guards in the existing facts DSL expression grammar (holon/gen/machine.py Machine.ex), so the back end and the proof generators stay unchanged.
4. Unsupported statements (loops with storage writes, external calls with callbacks) become coverage-debt entries with src spans.
5. Add tests_m2/test_extract_transitions.py: the extracted guards of the 8 M1 actions match the hand-written M1 guards up to the abstraction map. Every mismatch is listed in the PR, never suppressed.

items.item: View calls -> LOAD edges
items.evidence: The facts DSL has no edge kinds. Machine (holon/gen/machine.py) knows actions, defs and observers only. Views appear only as hand-written 'observers' (lci_of, csr_last, kappa, new_hdr) in morph_rollup.json; proveCommittedBatchState (view) is listed in coverage.debt.
items.gap: The §4 diagram has LOAD edges (Def 4.2), which are needed for E2 evidence ('written via p, read via q') and for PAR between store and load paths. No LOAD edges are extracted or represented.
items.proposed_work:
1. Extend the extracted facts (holon-facts/0.3) with an 'edges' list whose kinds are {CODEC, HASH, STORE, LOAD, CONS, TRANS, MIG}.
2. In holon/frontends/solidity/transitions.py, emit each view/pure external function and each internal _load* helper (e.g. _loadBatchHeader) as a LOAD edge with its src span.
3. Make holon/gen/machine.py compile LOAD edges to Bend defs over the state, alongside the observers.

items.item: keccak256 / blobhash / verifier calls -> commitment edges
items.evidence: Hashes and commitments are hand-picked stand-ins. The builtin 'agg' in holon/gen/machine.py is Nat.add(AGG_BASE, b_enc(xs)), with b_enc built on the Cantor pairing b_pair. blob_hash is a hand-written def; the verifier is an oracle, 'accepts iff proof == 1' (abstractions[6]). committedBatches is omitted under a CF premise (abstractions[1-2]). The facts have no 'commitments' (Cm) component.
items.gap: The whitepaper wants every keccak256, blobhash and verifier call site extracted as a HASH/commitment edge. These sites define Cm, which FACT obligations and CF premises are indexed by.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/frontends/solidity/transitions.py, recognise keccak256(...), blobhash(i) and calls through verifier interfaces (from the AST FunctionCall names and Yul builtins).
2. Emit HASH/COMMIT edges in the extracted facts with their input carriers (the memory layout from §10.2 when the preimage is a memory range) and a CF set name.
3. Have the model generator compile each one to a declared hash parameter (see the Appendix D item), not to a concrete injective function.
items.depends_on: External functions -> TRANS edges; Layout extraction

items.item: Loop bounds -> cost terms (c0 + sum c_l * iters_l(s))
items.evidence: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json 'disch' has only per-action unit costs (sendMessage 1, commitBatchWithProof 1000) and a delay. A grep for gas|iters finds nothing in holon/ or spec/. The 4 loops in Rollup.sol (while at :444; for at :489, :744, :936) are not represented.
items.gap: TRANS edges must carry cost terms derived from loop bounds, compared against the gas limit G (Def 4.2, Appendix D 'Cost'). This is the input to DISCH's 'gas on constraints' defects.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/frontends/solidity/transitions.py, extract each loop's bound expression over state and inputs (e.g. lastCommittedBatchIndex - lastFinalizedBatchIndex at :489, _numL1Messages at :936) and its per-iteration gas, using solc --gas or forge gas snapshots of a generated micro-harness.
2. Emit cost: {c0, terms: [{coef, iters_expr, src}]} on each TRANS edge.
3. Make holon/gen/machine.py emit cost_<a>(state, inputs) as a Bend def, so DISCH and refutation can compare it against G.

items.item: Straight-line mstore/mload sequences -> layouts
items.evidence: facts/morph_header.json functions.enc_sol.ops (mstore, mstore8) are hand-transcribed. Their sources cite 'bundle_lines' from the audit bundle, not repo lines (extraction.line_note). The real code is Rollup.sol:330-350, which calls BatchHeaderCodecV0.store* (BatchHeaderCodecV0.sol:133-211, each one inline-assembly mstore/mstore8 with shl(192, x)). The solc AST holds these Yul calls, but nothing parses them. facts/ is frozen.
items.gap: Layouts should be computed from the code's Yul by recognising mstore(b+o, shl(8(32-w), x)) and mstore8. Today the shl semantics are pre-digested by hand into field+zeros sources.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/solidity/layout_extract.py. It inlines internal library calls such as BatchHeaderCodecV0.storeX(_batchPtr, v) into one straight-line Yul sequence. It recognises mstore(add(p,o), shl(k,x)) as w = 32 - k/8 field bytes followed by zeros, mstore(add(p,o), x) as 32 field bytes, and mstore8(p, x) as 1 byte. It tracks mload(0x40) for p and records version-conditional header lengths (V0 249 / V1 257) from the if-branch on the version.
2. Output ops in the existing facts format, into spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json.
3. Add tests_m2/test_layout_extracted.py: holon.layout.layout over the extracted facts must equal the layout over the frozen facts/morph_header.json for versions 0-2 (Appendix C). Any difference is a finding about the hand-written facts or an extractor bug, and is reported.

items.item: Go frontend via go/ssa: binary.BigEndian / constant-offset copy / append chains -> codecs
items.evidence: facts/morph_header.json enc_go_v0 and enc_go_v1 (ops copy, put_uint64_be, set_byte) are hand-written. The real code is /root/work/morph/common/batch/batch_header.go:212-256, straight-line binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(batchBytes[1:], ...) and copy(batchBytes[25:], ...). No Go extractor exists (grep found nothing). Go 1.24.7 is installed. golang.org/x/tools is not in /root/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/x/, but proxy.golang.org is reachable (x/tools @latest is v0.52.0). Module deps for common/ (morph-l2/go-ethereum, morph-da-codec) are cached; node/ deps such as the tendermint fork are not.
items.gap: Go codecs should be extracted from SSA. There is no SSA dump and no recogniser.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/go/ssadump/ (main.go, go.mod and go.sum pinning golang.org/x/tools to a fixed version). It loads packages with go/packages from a scratch go.work (the same layout replay.replay_go builds), builds SSA, and for each named function prints a deterministic JSON of instructions (sorted by position): calls to encoding/binary.bigEndian.PutUint64, copy builtins with constant-offset slice operands, append chains, and IndexAddr/Slice sites.
2. Add holon/frontends/go/extract.py, which turns that JSON into facts ops (put_uint64_be, copy, set_byte) with real file:line spans.
3. Add `tools/setup_env.sh --extract`, which runs go mod download for the pinned x/tools.
4. Add tests_m2/test_extract_go.py: the extracted enc_go_v0/v1 must give the same holon.layout as the frozen facts.

items.item: Go index and slice sites -> partiality annotations
items.evidence: The partiality of the Go getters is hand-modelled through the guard ok_go and dec_go getters (offset/width) in facts/morph_header.json. The real getters (batch_header.go:83-192, e.g. binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[249:257])) can panic on short input; no annotation is extracted. M0 BEND_NOTES §4.5 notes that undefinedness must propagate, and refute.py:subterms works around this.
items.gap: Every index or slice expression should yield a definedness side condition (panic on out-of-range) on its edge. This is what A2 hostile-input checks (§9.5) rely on.
items.proposed_work:
1. In holon/frontends/go/ssadump, emit each IndexAddr/Index/Slice with its bound operands.
2. In holon/frontends/go/extract.py, attach 'partial': [{cond: len(b) >= hi, src}] to the edge.
3. Make holon/gen/model.py emit an explicit undefined result (the existing 0xDEAD convention) when the condition fails, so refutation finds panics as definedness mismatches.
4. Add tests_m2: the extracted dec_go partiality must match the hand-written ok_go on every length in refute.length_constants ±1.

items.item: Go slice headers -> backing-identity facts for OWN
items.evidence: spec/M1/facts/morph_batchdata.json is a hand-written heap model. Slices are (backing, offset, len, cap); the Go 1.24 growth policy is an oracle with a class table truncated to 512 B (abstractions[1]). Only Append and TxsPayloadV2 are modelled (coverage.debt lists Encode, DataHash, ...). holon/gen/machine.py has hand-written builtins b_go_append_slice, b_go_append_heap and b_go_read. L_own_txspayload is REFUTED and replays on the real Go code.
items.gap: Backing identity should come from SSA (Slice/MakeSlice/append results, and which values alias which backing array), not from a hand-built heap model of one type. The size-class oracle is truncated, so bigger slices are modelled wrongly (stated in abstractions[1]).
items.proposed_work:
1. Extend holon/frontends/go/ssadump to emit, for each function, its slice-producing instructions and the alias set of each result (go/pointer or a simple intraprocedural points-to over SSA values).
2. In holon/frontends/go/own.py, generate the holon-facts heap-machine actions (append, read, view-return) for every exported method of a struct with []byte fields, plus a 'views' list of returned slices that alias a field.
3. Generate the full runtime/sizeclasses.go table as data, from the Go toolchain source in GOROOT, instead of truncating it. Keep the BendTT size limit in mind (M1_REPORT §2.6) by moving the table out of the state into a def.

items.item: Go pipelines -> consumers (Cn)
items.evidence: There is exactly one hand-written consumer: morph_rollup.json consumers.blobs_of ('the blob sidecar a commit transaction delivers to L2 derivation'). The derivation pipeline in /root/work/morph/node/derivation (batch_info.go, blobs.go, beacon.go, ...) is not modelled. The §4.6 payload and derivation pipelines (builder -> payload -> compressed -> blobs -> beta -> b57; blobs -> stream -> derived blocks) are absent.
items.gap: Consumers should be the extracted Go pipelines from committed data to security-relevant outputs. FACT needs them (ker(m) ⊆ ker(c)).
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/go/consumers.py. Starting from functions that read L1 data (node/derivation/*.go: blob fetch, batch_info parse), follow SSA call chains to derived-block outputs, and emit CONS edges with their input carriers and partiality.
2. Straight-line codec fragments inside them go through the Go translator. The rest is recorded as coverage debt.
3. The node module needs the tendermint fork and other deps that are not in /root/go/pkg/mod. Add a pinned `go mod download` step to `tools/setup_env.sh --extract`.

items.item: Linking: ABI bindings, shared constants (249, 257, Z, 4096*31), event schemas
items.evidence: Nothing links the languages. The M0 header model (gen/M0/model/morph_header.bend, 257 U32 cells) and the M1 state machine (gen/M1/model/morph_rollup.bend, where b_hdr_of returns a 7-tuple [ver, tot, n, hb, prev, post, lbn] of Nat tokens) are disjoint models of the same header. The constants are typed by hand: length_by_version 249/257 in facts; params Z=1 is a token, documented in constants_doc. The Go ABI bindings exist (/root/work/morph/bindings/bindings/rollup.go), and so do the events (IRollup.sol:74-121: CommitBatch, RevertBatch, FinalizeBatch), but no code reads them. replay.py only copies bindings/ for go test.
items.gap: The diagram should join Solidity and Go carriers through the ABI (calldata structs ↔ Go binding structs), shared constants and event schemas. Without that, PAR between the state machine and the codecs (e.g. committedBatches = keccak(header bytes)) cannot be stated.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/link.py. It parses the solc ABI (from the compile step) and the Go binding structs (from SSA types in bindings/bindings/rollup.go), and matches function inputs (BatchDataInput fields) to Go struct fields by ABI name and type.
2. Collect constant declarations on both sides (Solidity constant state vars, Go const blocks); emit 'shared_constants' with both src spans when the values are equal, and a linking discrepancy when they are not.
3. Map events to the Go log decoders.
4. Make holon/gen/machine.py able to import a codec model, so the state machine's header is the M0 byte layout instead of b_hdr_of tokens.
5. Add a tests_m2 check that every linked pair has a PAR obligation candidate.
items.depends_on: Solidity frontend infrastructure; Go frontend via go/ssa

items.item: Deployment history -> migrations and in-flight types (proxy upgrades, reinitializer versions, storage diffs)
items.evidence: Two migrations in spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json are hand-written: 'legacy' (CSR zeroed) and 'eta2' (initialize2, Rollup.sol:188-195). The whitepaper's eta3, eta4, eta_enq and eta_BVH are not modelled; initialize3 and initialize4 are in coverage.debt. Rollup.sol has reinitializer(2/3/4) at :188, :199, :209. Raw material exists: the morph checkout is non-shallow (git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository = false), 38 commits touch Rollup.sol, and contracts/storage-layout/archive/Rollup.pre-submitter.json is a historical layout. No code diffs storage layouts or tracks upgrades.
items.gap: Migrations should be derived from the upgrade history: reinitializer bodies become MIG edges, and storage-layout diffs between deployed versions become in-flight types (fields added, retyped or reinterpreted).
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/solidity/history.py. For a list of pinned historical commits (spec/M2/deployments.json: commit, proxy, implementation, block), compile each version (git show into a scratch dir, never touching the checkout), diff the storageLayout JSONs (added, removed or retyped slots), and extract the reinitializer(k) bodies as MIG edges with their effects.
2. Emit migrations plus in_flight_types into the extracted facts.
3. Validate against the hand-written eta2 and legacy migrations in tests_m2.
4. Get the deployment block and implementation addresses from contracts/deploy/*.ts and on-chain proxy events. This needs RPC access: record it as an input file, not a live query, for determinism.

items.item: Deterministic translators (straight-line Yul and Go-SSA -> Bend), validated per instance by replay
items.evidence: The deterministic back ends exist and are byte-checked by G1 (holon/gate.py): holon/gen/model.py (facts ops -> Bend put/overlay chains) and holon/gen/machine.py (guarded-command DSL -> decide_<a>/exec_<a>). Their input is hand-written, not translated from Yul or SSA. machine.py also has Morph-specific builtins (win_at, win_last, nth_ch, set_ch, bump_f, any_open, clear_chs, zero_csr, set_last_csr, tags_exact, hdr_of; Machine.builtin 'fixed' dict), so the 'generic' compiler carries target knowledge. Replay validates the model as a whole, not per fragment: holon/mreplay.py random_corpus, 300 traces and 2,432 steps with 0 disagreements (replay/M1/report.json). There is no historical-input corpus.
items.gap: The whitepaper calls for syntactic, deterministic Yul/SSA→Bend translation with replay of each translated fragment. That is the M2 exit criterion: zero unexplained disagreements over a historical window. Today the translation step is human.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/translate_yul.py and translate_ssa.py. They map supported straight-line Yul and SSA instruction subsets (arithmetic with width, mstore/mload, sload/sstore, comparisons, revert) to facts-DSL expressions.
2. Move the Morph-specific builtins out of holon/gen/machine.py into per-target defs written in the DSL (spec/<M>/facts defs), so extracted facts compile with no target code in holon/.
3. Add holon/replay_fragments.py. For each translated fragment, generate a Foundry micro-harness (for library or internal functions, via a test contract that exposes them) or a Go test calling the real function on N inputs (grammar, boundary and historical). Compare against the compiled model through holon/model_eval.CompiledModel, and write per-edge refinement records to results/<M>/refinement/<edge>.json.
4. Add a historical corpus fetcher, tools/fetch_history.py, writing replay/M2/history/*.json (commitBatch calldata and blobs where retained), pinned by block range and hashed.
items.depends_on: Solidity frontend infrastructure; Go frontend via go/ssa

items.item: Coverage debt: unsupported fragments recorded, never approximated silently (feeds G8)
items.evidence: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json coverage.modelled/debt and morph_batchdata.json coverage.debt are hand-written lists (e.g. 'importGenesisBatch', 'initialize3', 'claimReward', 'withdrawalRoots'). holon/gate.py CHECK_ORDER is GENV, G2, G1, G3, G5, G11, G7, G4, with no G8. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §1 says 'G8–G10 arrive with extraction (M2)'.
items.gap: A coverage report should be computed from code: every in-scope function, branch and storage family either mapped into 𝔇 or listed as debt with a src span. G8 should check that the report is attached.
items.proposed_work:
1. Have each frontend emit coverage.json: every AST/SSA element in scope, with status mapped, debt or out_of_scope and a reason.
2. Add holon/coverage.py, which merges the per-frontend reports into results/<M>/coverage.json.
3. Add G8 to holon/gate.py: the report exists, matches a fresh extraction byte for byte, and every debt entry has a src span. Count debt in summary.json.
items.depends_on: Solidity frontend infrastructure; Go frontend via go/ssa

items.item: Layout Λ: byte -> (field, k) | const | unknown; EVM mstore (32-byte write, later writes override, dirty memory) and mstore8
items.evidence: holon/layout.py:layout initialises EVM memory as ['unknown'] (dirty memory) and applies ops in program order (override). holon/facts.py OP_WIDTH {mstore: 32, mstore8: 1, set_byte: 1, put_uint64_be: 8} and src_cells implement the field+zeros semantics. Tests: tests/test_10_layout.py test_layouts_match_oracle, test_layouts_follow_mutated_facts, test_overlapping_writes_last_wins; tests/test_01_reference.py test_layouts_match_appendix_c (Appendix C reproduced). CLI: `python -m holon layout FN V`.
items.gap: None for the algebra itself. The shl(8(32-w), x) pattern is not recognised from code but pre-digested in the facts; that is covered by the extraction item.
items.proposed_work: No change needed. Keep holon/layout.py as the consumer of extracted ops (see 'Straight-line mstore/mload sequences -> layouts').

items.item: EVM calldatacopy: positions map to calldata
items.evidence: holon/facts.py OP_WIDTH has no calldatacopy, and check_op_width raises 'unsupported op' for anything outside OP_WIDTH except copy. A grep for calldatacopy across holon/, facts/ and spec/ returns nothing. src_cells supports only field, zeros and const.
items.gap: Λ cells cannot refer to calldata positions, so layouts built by copying calldata (e.g. header loading and payload paths that copy calldata into memory) are inexpressible.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add a cell kind ['calldata', arg, k] and an op calldatacopy {dst, arg, src_off, len} to holon/layout.py and holon/facts.py (holon-facts/0.3; the frozen facts/ stays at 0.1).
2. Extend holon/gen/model.py so the encoder takes the calldata argument as a byte-list parameter and calldatacopy becomes put(m, dst, slice(cd, off, len)).
3. Add unit tests in tests_m2/test_layout_calldatacopy.py (tests/ is frozen).

items.item: Go PutUint64 (8 positions) and copy (32 positions)
items.evidence: holon/facts.py OP_WIDTH['put_uint64_be'] = 8; copy is allowed with any width (check_op_width). Go buffers start as const 0 (holon/layout.py, lang 'go-bytes'). holon/gen/model.py _put_chain emits put(m, off, [...]) over zeros(len). L_rt_go_v0/v1/v2 and L_par_hdr_v0/v1 are PROVED (results/M0).
items.gap: None. copy is more general than the whitepaper's 32 positions.
items.proposed_work: No change needed.

items.item: Getters recover a field iff its positions map to it in order (E1 evidence from the layout algebra)
items.evidence: holon/layout.py has only layout() and diff(). There is no getter-recovery function; a grep for 'recover|E1|evidence|inverse' in holon/*.py finds only unrelated hits. The decoder getters (facts/morph_header.json dec_go.getters offset/width) are hand-specified and never checked against Λ. Nothing computes E1 evidence (Def 4.5).
items.gap: The whitepaper uses getter recovery to decide whether an encoder/decoder pair is mutually inverse on a field (E1). This is how PAR cycles get strong evidence.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/layout.py:recovers(layout, getter) -> bool: true iff positions [off, off+w) map to (field, 0..w-1) in order.
2. Add evidence(enc_layout, dec_getters) -> {field: 'E1' | None}.
3. Emit the evidence into a generated results/<M>/evidence.json and consume it in law generation (§10.3, other reader).
4. Add tests_m2: for the frozen header facts, every dec_go getter at versions 0 and 1 recovers its field from enc_sol and enc_go_v*, except fields that differ by version.

items.item: Decidable layout equality in O(L)
items.evidence: holon/layout.py:diff does one linear pass and also reports a length mismatch. It is used only by the CLI (holon/__main__.py 'layout') and tests. The pipeline decides equality by Bend evaluation instead (open_refl).
items.gap: Nothing feeds the decision procedure's result into evidence or law selection. That is minor and tied to getter recovery and §10.3.
items.proposed_work: Use layout.diff in the evidence and obligation pass (holon/evidence.py, new) to pre-classify candidate PAR pairs before emitting laws.

items.item: Layout facts emitted as Bend definitions; layout lemmas proved by evaluation over symbolic fields
items.evidence: holon/gen/model.py emits a Hdr record of U32 cells and encoders as put/overlay chains over dirty memory (List.replicate(U32, size, 0xDEAD)) or zeros. holon/gen/proofs.py open_refl opens the record binder and closes the goal with {==} (proof by computation over symbolic cells). L_par_hdr_v0 and L_par_hdr_v1 are PROVED and BendTT-checked (results/M0/*.json kernel.verdict 'checked'). Caveat: holon/layout.py (Python) and holon/gen/model.py (Bend) are two independent interpreters of the same facts ops; no test cross-checks them directly (test_10 compares layout.py with the oracle, test_20 compares model eval with the oracle).
items.gap: There are no standalone reusable layout lemmas (Appendix H core/ 'layout lemmas'); each PAR law re-proves its layout by evaluation. Acceptable at the current scale.
items.proposed_work: Optional: add tests_m2/test_layout_vs_model.py, which evaluates each compiled encoder on a symbolic-marker header (distinct byte per cell) and checks that the output matches holon.layout cell by cell. That ties the two interpreters together.

items.item: Layout facts emitted as solver queries for refutation
items.evidence: There is no SMT code anywhere: a grep for 'z3|smt|qf_ufbv|cvc5|bitwuzla|solver' in holon/*.py and holon/js/*.mjs finds nothing. z3, cvc5 and bitwuzla are not installed (which: MISSING; python -c 'import z3': ModuleNotFoundError).
items.gap: Layouts should also be emitted as bitvector constraints, so that a solver can find inputs separating two layouts, or a calldata/memory layout reaching a target byte pattern.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/smt/layout.py. For each encoder at each version, emit SMT-LIB2: (declare-const f_<field> (_ BitVec 8w)), output bytes as extracts or constants, and dirty memory as fresh unconstrained bytes.
2. A query is (assert (distinct out_a out_b)) under the law's pins.
3. Run it through the shared solver runner (see the SMT engine item). The model only proposes candidates: holon/refute.py evaluates them on the compiled model and they go through the counter-law path.

items.item: Proof generator: layout equality by evaluation
items.evidence: holon/gen/proofs.py open_refl (open record binders, then {==}) and version_split (case split on the version byte 0n..Kn, (K+1)n+p, with a lemma). GENERATORS dispatch on statement shape, never on law ids. L_par_hdr_v0/v1 and L_rt_go_v* are PROVED; MUT3 reaches PROVED via version_split (tests/test_31_mutations.py).
items.gap: None.
items.proposed_work: No change needed.

items.item: Proof generator: UNDO dead residue via bisimulation step lemmas for 'equal outside Res', per action
items.evidence: holon/gen/mproofs.py noninterference. Per action, it generalises over decide_<a> (which reads only the guard fields), rewrites with the hypothesis proj(s1) == proj(s2) (the erased view = Res) and inducts on the trace. L_undo_CSR and L_undo_BD are PROVED unbounded and dual-kernel (results/M1). Gate canaries 'erase_live' ×12 are rejected (tests_m1/test_m1_gate.py test_canaries). MUT4 turns L_undo_CSR into REFUTED (tests_m1/test_m1_mutations.py).
items.gap: Res is a whole state field: the shadow lists s_csr/s_bd, a representation the hand-written facts chose to make non-interference structural (M1_REPORT §3). It is not 'equal outside {CSR_i, BD_i}' at a symbolic index i. The core lemmas (CORE string in mproofs.py) are re-emitted in every PROOF file instead of living in a shared kernel-checked core library (Appendix H core/ 'bisimulation kit').
items.proposed_work:
1. Once extraction yields raw index-keyed families (no shadow lists), extend noninterference to an index-relative relation: equal everywhere except family F at indices > LCI. Per-action lemmas will need list lemmas over set_d and nth_d (already present in machine.py PRELUDE).
2. Move the CORE lemmas into a generated gen/<M>/core/core.bend that every PROOF.bend imports, so they are checked once per run.

items.item: Proof generator: SYM per-action generator lemmas (equivariance)
items.evidence: holon/gen/mproofs.py GENERATORS = evaluate, nat_split, noninterference, deadline, chain_revert; there is no equivariance class. The only SYM law, L_sym_omega, is REFUTED via the counter generator (results/M1/L_sym_omega.json attempts: refute, counter-law). A grep for equivar|symmetr in holon/ finds nothing.
items.gap: There is no way to PROVE a symmetry family (τ, ι, π, μ) per action, so no split A_eq can be certified.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add mproofs.equivariance: for a law ∀s, a. step(g·a, g·s) == g·step(a, s), where g is a generated def in LAWS.bend (time shift on Time-sorted fields, index shift on Idx-sorted fields, principal permutation within a role), emit a per-action lemma.
2. Generalise over decide_<a> as noninterference does, and prove decide_<a>(g·reads) == decide_<a>(reads) by rewriting with arithmetic lemmas (core_le_add_l and similar, extended with shift-invariance of <, ≤, ==).
3. Dispatch on statement shape only.
4. Add canaries that mutate g (e.g. shift one extra field).

items.item: Proof generator: NAT per entry point (native equivalence across migrations)
items.evidence: There is no NAT proof class in holon/gen/mproofs.py. L_nat_eta2 is REFUTED only (counter). docs/M1_REPORT.md §7: 'Reachability invariants (D4) and NAT laws other than η₂ ... need induction over Reach'. The model has migration defs (mig_legacy, mig_eta2 used in holon/mreplay.py model_logs), but there is no Reach predicate and no per-entry-point lemma.
items.gap: NAT obligations (entry points × in-flight types) cannot be PROVED; only refuted.
items.proposed_work:
1. Generate an inductive Reach_k predicate per state version in holon/gen/machine.py (§8.3; coordinate with the reader covering §8).
2. Add mproofs.nat_entry: for each public action a and migration m, prove obs(step(a, m(s))) == obs(step(a, native(s))) for s satisfying Reach. Do this by generalising over decide_a on both sides and rewriting with the migration's field-wise effects. Fall back to UNKNOWN with the failing per-action lemma recorded.

items.item: Proof generator: DISCH strategy programs and invariant lemmas for blocking
items.evidence: holon/gen/mproofs.py. 'evaluate' takes a strategy from explore.mjs strategies() and checks it by computation; 'nat_split' gives L_disch_delay_nofree; 'deadline' gives L_disch_stale; 'chain_revert' gives L_disch_stale_commit. All are PROVED (results/M1). deadline depends on _kappa_shape, which only matches kappa = b && (x + get(nth_ch(chs, i), f)) < t, built on the Morph builtin nth_ch. Profile points are checked at one hand-chosen representative state s* (M1_REPORT §5).
items.gap: Invariant synthesis is limited to one guard shape. Strategies are certified at one state rather than per guard class. There is no general frame/monotone/clear classification per effect.
items.proposed_work:
1. Generalise _kappa_shape into a classifier over arbitrary conjunctions of atoms on state fields: for each action effect, decide frame (field untouched), monotone (only increases a field on the right of <) or clear. Emit one preservation lemma per (atom, action).
2. Take the strategy start states from the §10.7 guard-class abstraction (other reader), not from a single s*.
3. Keep dispatch on shape only.

items.item: Agents (Bender, coding agents) fill remaining goals; only kernel-accepted proof files matter
items.evidence: holon/pipeline.py prove() and holon/mpipeline.py run_m1 only try the built-in generators, and UNKNOWN is terminal (scope 'bounded', bound recorded). There is no intake path for externally authored proofs (Appendix H 'proofs/  PROOF files (untrusted inputs)'): grep for 'proofs/' in holon/*.py finds only gen paths. A grep for agent|bender in holon/ finds only AGENTS.md references in docstrings.
items.gap: There is no mechanism for an untrusted agent to submit a PROOF.bend for a frozen law and have it promoted after kernel checks.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/intake.py and a CLI `python -m holon intake --milestone M --law L --proof path`. It re-emits LAWS.bend from the frozen IR (never from the agent), copies the agent's PROOF.bend into proofs/<M>/<law>/, rejects escape hatches (bend.escape_hatches) and checks that law_names == [expected]. It then runs bend.check and check_verdict and records the attempt with generator 'external:<sha256 of proof>'.
2. In mpipeline/pipeline, try the generators first and then proofs/<M>/<law>/PROOF.bend if present.
3. Have G5 re-check external proofs and G4 canaries run against them as well.

items.item: SMT refutation engine over QF_UFBV with ground injectivity over the query's own hash terms
items.evidence: which z3 cvc5 bitwuzla yices boolector: all MISSING. python -c 'import z3' gives ModuleNotFoundError. No solver code (grep over holon/ for z3|smt|solver is empty). pip dry-run shows z3-solver 5.1.0.0 and cvc5 1.4.2 are installable through the proxy.
items.gap: There is no general refutation search. Every refutation comes from enumeration over hand-made candidate spaces, so deep or arithmetic-heavy witnesses (large Nat values, specific hash relationships) are out of reach.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/smt/encode.py, which compiles the facts DSL (the same expression grammar as holon/gen/machine.py Machine.ex) to SMT-LIB2 bitvectors. Widths come from ABI types; checked arithmetic becomes a revert predicate and unchecked arithmetic becomes bvadd wraparound. The action sequence is unrolled for k steps from s0 or from a symbolic State. Hash calls become one declare-fun K per hash, with ground injectivity asserted pairwise over the K-terms in this query only: CF(K, S_query), per Appendix D and Cor 6.16.
2. Add holon/smt/run.py: pinned z3 (requirements-extract.txt z3-solver==5.1.0.0), smt.random_seed=0, a per-obligation timeout from config, and deterministic model extraction.
3. The solver model is only a candidate. Decode it to IR values, evaluate it on the compiled model (CompiledMachine.evaluate or refute.evaluate) and emit the counter-law (mproofs.counter / proofs.counter). AGENTS rule 5 holds: the model, not the solver, decides.
4. Add the attempt kind 'smt' with its query sha256 to the records.

items.item: Refutation encodings in the model: hashes as uninterpreted K with ground CF, Z := VH(0), checked/unchecked arithmetic, time, cost
items.evidence: Hash: the builtin 'agg' in holon/gen/machine.py is Nat.add(AGG_BASE, b_enc(xs)), with b_enc built on the Cantor pairing b_pair. That is a concrete, globally injective function (morph_rollup.json abstractions[5]: 'models CF(keccak256, S) for every finite S'). Z is the token param Z=1, not VH(0) with top byte 0x01. Arithmetic is unbounded Nat (Nat.add/Nat.sub in Machine.ex); there are no widths or bitvector wraparound. Time is a 'wait dt' action (non-decreasing): matches. Cost is not encoded (see the cost-term item).
items.gap: The whitepaper withdraws global injectivity (Thm 6.15). Hashes should be uninterpreted, with CF premises local to each statement. A concrete injective stand-in hides every collision-dependent behaviour and makes PROVED laws silently rely on global CF. Unbounded Nat misses width-wrap defects in unchecked blocks (Rollup.sol:324 unchecked _totalL1MessagesPoppedOverall +=).
items.proposed_work:
1. Add a hash-parameter mode to holon/gen/machine.py: K is a law binder of function type, with CF(K, S_law) as an explicit premise (IR 0.3 binder type 'Fn'). The concrete 'agg' stays only in the explorer's compiled model as a search heuristic.
2. Add width-annotated arithmetic ('+w', '-w' with mod 2^w for unchecked blocks; a revert reason for checked overflow) to the facts DSL and machine.py, with widths from storage and ABI types.
3. New laws go in a new milestone. Do not rewrite M1 statements; follow the §9.4 strengthening rules.
items.depends_on: SMT QF_UFBV refutation engine; Storage families -> state carriers

items.item: Bounded exhaustive enumeration over small domains and short action sequences in the compiled model
items.evidence: holon/js/explore.mjs runs a breadth-first search for prefixes (prefixDepth 3, maxPrefixes 3000, deduplicated by state), a divergence search (suffixDepth 4, maxNodes 400000), Nat binders 0..natMax=5 plus premise-solved values, and a strategy search for exists laws. The action alphabet comes from holon/js/policy_lib.mjs, which is hand-written and Morph-specific ('Search policy for the Morph rollup machine': fixed who per action, fresh = 100+10*(lci+1), blob = 7+10*(lci+1), deadline-derived waits) plus batchdataPolicy. It is not an exhaustive domain. holon/refute.py (M0) raises Unsupported for more than one binder ('refuter handles one binder in M0') and uses fixed candidate lists. When the search exhausts, the record says scope 'bounded' with the bound string, but there is no exhaustive-scope claim.
items.gap: The enumeration does not cover a declared finite domain, and its candidate generator is target-specific code under holon/. With extracted facts (new field names) the policy breaks. No bounded-exhaustive result such as 'no counterexample for all sequences ≤ k over domain D' is recorded as a scoped certificate.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/js/policy_gen.mjs, which derives candidate actions from the facts alone: per input type, the ABI range boundaries (0, 1, max, max-1), the constants in that action's guards ±1, the current values of Idx-sorted state fields ±1, and deadlines from Time-sorted fields minus t, ±1.
2. Move policy_lib.mjs's Morph heuristics to spec/M1/policy.mjs as an optional, untrusted hint file named by facts.policy.
3. Add a 'domain' mode in explore.mjs: when every input has a finite declared domain, enumerate the full product to depth k and return {exhausted: true, domain, k}. Record it as scope: bounded(k, domain) in UNKNOWN records.
4. Generalise holon/refute.py to n binders via a product of candidate spaces.

items.item: GPU (or native) targets for bounded enumeration where the fragment is supported
items.evidence: Every evaluation runs through `bend model.bend -o model.mjs` in node (holon/model_eval.py CompiledModel.build, holon/mpipeline.py CompiledMachine.build). `bend --help` shows that -o can also produce a binary or C, but it is unused. No nvcc or nvidia-smi exists in the container; gcc and clang are present; nproc = 4.
items.gap: There is no high-throughput enumerator: no GPU, and not even native C.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/enum/native.py. It builds the model with `bend model.bend -o model.c`, wrapped in a generated Bend main that reads an action sequence from stdin; no foreign imports in Bend (AGENTS rule 3). It then compiles with gcc -O2.
2. Add a C driver, holon/enum/driver.c (outside Bend, untrusted), that enumerates action sequences in parallel processes, deterministic by sharding on index.
3. Differential check: on a fixed sample, results must match the .mjs model before native results are trusted.
4. Add a CUDA path only when nvcc is detected. Record the engine in the attempts.

items.item: Grammar- and sort-boundary fuzzing of the compiled model
items.evidence: holon/refute.py, M0 only: version_constants and length_constants ±1, structured fills (zeros, ones, 0x01, one field 0xff, counting), and RANDOM_HEADERS = 48 seeded headers (SEED 20261010). Bytes candidates are versions × lengths × (zeros, ones, 1 random). M1: holon/mreplay.py random_corpus (seed 20261011, random walks over the policy with perturbed who/idx/parent) is used only for refinement replay, never for refutation. There are no carrier grammars and no coverage feedback.
items.gap: There is no grammar-based generator for carrier types (records, byte strings with structure, action sequences), no use of extracted sentinel constants, and no fuzzing mode in the M1 refuter.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/fuzz.py: seeded, grammar-based generators derived from facts types (Header fields, List<Nat>, ABI structs) plus sort-boundary values (0, 1, max, max-1, every guard constant).
2. Use guard-outcome coverage as feedback: decide_<a> already returns which require failed, through the obs reason codes.
3. Feed it into explore.mjs as an extra candidate source ('fuzz' budget). Share the generators with §8.7 replay source 1 (inputs sampled from carrier grammars).
4. Keep it deterministic: fixed seed and iteration count from config, with results independent of wall clock.

items.evidence: A single hand-written law, laws/M1/L_sym_omega.json, fixes the pair by the is_commitBatchWithProof and is_challengeState premises and requires runs_ok for both orders. It is REFUTED and replayed (replay/M1/report.json). Nothing enumerates the other pairs, checks different principal classes (facts actions[*].principal is free text) or filters by sink-reaching registers. There is no disabling-race classification.

Enumerate action pairs whose principal classes differ (with principal classes as structured data in the facts); compute sink-reaching registers by backward dataflow from commitments, consumers and fund transfers over Machine.reads and the write sets. Emit L_sym_omega-shaped IR laws per pair, with the claim restricted to the sink projection.

items.evidence: No code. The whitepaper's Morph instances (enq = 0 as τ sentinel; address(0) as π role) are not represented; the queue's 'enq' is modelled but no translation family is checked.

items.item: Bounded model checking over TRANS edges to a reachable path to the witness state (environment moves, principal constraints)
items.evidence: M1 witnesses are traces from s0. explore.mjs prefixes() keeps only successful actions, and every REFUTED M1 witness is a list or run (results/M1/*.json witness kinds), so it is reachable by construction. Environment moves (wait dt) and principals (who) are chosen by the hand-written policy_lib.mjs, not constrained by the facts' principal classes. State binders can be filled by perturb() (explore.mjs), which yields unreachable states; no reachability check exists for those. M0 header witnesses have no path to a public entry point: replay/M0/report.json has L_par_hdr_v2 and L_par_hdr_ssvh solidity 'not_applicable' ('needs a full commitBatch deployment ... M1'). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4 item 5 planned to close this in M1, but it was not done.
items.gap: There is no solver-based or exhaustive BMC that searches for a path to a given witness state. Witnesses over arbitrary states or inputs (M0 headers) are not concretised to entry-point schedules.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/bmc.py, using the SMT encoder (unroll k TRANS steps from s0, time monotone, who ∈ the principal class of each action). Goal: the final state or the call input equals the witness (e.g. a commitBatch whose built header has version 2 for L_par_hdr_v2). Fall back to explore.mjs breadth-first search with a goal predicate.
2. Validate the path on the compiled model, then replay.
3. Immediate M0 debt: generate commit-path traces for L_par_hdr_v2 and L_par_hdr_ssvh through the M1 machine (commitBatch ver=2, which policy_lib already proposes) and replay them through HolonTraceReplay.t.sol, updating replay/M0/report.json with a witness-hash-bound entry.

items.item: Path emitted as a test against the pinned implementation: a Foundry test for EVM, a Go test for the node
items.evidence: Solidity uses one generic data-driven harness, replay/M1/solidity/HolonTraceReplay.t.sol (273 lines, hand-written), fed by holon/mreplay.py encode_step. That function has a hard-coded Morph OPS table {commitBatch: 1, ..., '@legacy_eta2': 11} and a WIDTH-13 encoding; there are also oracle stand-ins for ISubmitter and IRollupVerifier. Go uses hand-written replay/M1/go/holon_own_test.go and replay/M0/go/holon_replay_test.go, which read the result records. No per-witness test file is emitted. Nothing is generated from the facts or ABI. There are no node (derivation) Go tests.
items.gap: Tests are not emitted per witness from facts and ABI. The harness and op mapping are Morph-specific code, so a second target (M4) would need a new hand-written harness.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/gen/foundry.py. It emits replay/<M>/solidity/Holon_<law>.t.sol deterministically per REFUTED witness, using the ABI and the action→function mapping produced by extraction (function selector, argument encoding from BatchDataInput, prank from the principal class, vm.warp from wait). It also emits a generic deploy fixture generated from the deploy scripts or initializer list.
2. Add holon/gen/gotest.py, which emits Go tests per witness for Go-side edges.
3. Replace mreplay.OPS and encode_step with the generated mapping.
4. Have G1 regenerate the emitted tests.

items.item: Outcome classification: replay success -> finding; replay failure -> model defect; known limitation
items.evidence: holon/mreplay.py main_replay_m1 sets status 'passed' iff every step agrees and the obstruction reproduces. Otherwise it prints 'MODEL DEFECT / NOT REPRODUCED' and exits 1. holon/replay.py has stamp_records and replay_status, binding replay to the witness sha256. Triage ('finding' / 'intent_question') comes from the hand-written config/triage.json. The 'known limitation' bin (a witness no public entry point produces) is never computed.
items.gap: There is no automatic three-bin filter. The known-limitation bin is missing, and findings are labelled by hand.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/filter.py, which writes results/<M>/filter.json. The bin is 'finding' if replay passed and the trace starts at s0 using public entry points only. It is 'model_defect' if any step disagrees. It is 'known_limitation' if BMC proves no public-entry path within bound k, or the witness needs a pseudo-step (e.g. '@legacy_eta2' storage emulation, which is currently counted as passed).
2. config/triage.json stays a human input for intent questions only.

items.item: Ranking: lexicographic by sink class, persistence, reach class, adversary cost; discharge profiles feed persistence

items.item: Obligation counts linear in the diagram

items.item: Proof checking: per-law cost bounded by the gate budget and parallel across files

There is no concurrent.futures or multiprocessing in holon/. G5 checks exit status and marker only, with no budget assertion. The seconds fields are recorded.

2. Run bend.check and check_verdict through concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor in pipeline, mpipeline and gate, collecting results in sorted law order for determinism.

items.item: Refutation budgeted per obligation, exhaustion recorded as UNKNOWN with what was tried
items.evidence: explore.mjs takes its budget from facts.search and req.budget (maxNodes 400000, plus the cutoff 'tried > maxNodes*4'). mpipeline.CompiledMachine.explore has a 3600 s subprocess timeout. UNKNOWN records get scope 'bounded' and bound = the description string (mpipeline.run_m1). In M0, refute.describe_space records the candidate space. There is no per-rule or per-obligation budget in config, no wall-clock budget recorded, and the exhaustion reason (node cap vs. space exhausted) is not distinguished.
items.gap: Budgets are global constants, not per obligation. Records do not say whether the search space was exhausted or the budget was hit.

summary:
Case-study gap map for whitepaper §11 (O1-O37, D1-D9, N1-N4, §11.5, §11.8) and Appendix A (F1-F14), checked against laws/M0, laws/M1, results/, replay/, spec/M1, docs/M1_REPORT.md and the pinned morph checkout at /root/work/morph (3e44e79). Read-only.

COVERAGE. 13 of the 37 obstructions have a law. 8 are fully covered: the law was mechanized, checked by both kernels and replayed on real code. 5 are partial. 24 have no law. Of the 9 discharged obligations, 2 are done, 1 is partial and 6 are missing. In Appendix A, only F4 and F6 are fully reproduced; F2, F5, F7, F9 and F12 are partial; F1, F3, F8, F10, F11, F13 and F14 have nothing. §11.7's claim "Reproduced: all of F1-F14" therefore does not yet hold for the mechanized system.

O-id -> law. Every law below was dual-kernel checked; replay is on morph 3e44e79:
- O1 -> L_dom_hdr (M0): REFUTED, replayed on Go and Solidity.
- O2 -> L_par_hdr_v2 (M0): REFUTED, replayed on Go only; the Solidity side is still not_applicable.
- O11 -> L_undo_BVH: REFUTED, replayed through Foundry.
- O12 -> L_undo_cancel: REFUTED, replayed. The intent contract is missing.
- O15 -> L_nat_eta2: REFUTED, added post hoc, replayed against emulated legacy storage.
- O19 -> L_sym_omega: REFUTED, replayed.
- O22 -> L_fact_Z: REFUTED, replayed.
- O26 -> L_tag_BVH: REFUTED. The replay only shows the contract accepting the trace.
- O27 -> L_sort_remaining: REFUTED, replayed (Panic 0x11).
- O31 -> L_disch_stale and L_disch_stale_commit: PROVED, unbounded. Only the blocking half is covered.
- O32 -> L_undo_BVH, shared with O11. It is an UNDO witness only; there is no DISCH non-dischargeability law.
- O33 -> L_disch_delay_nofree, L_disch_delay_pay and L_disch_delay_wait, plus L_disch_delay_prove (post hoc): all PROVED. These are profile points only; Pareto minimality and the write closure are not proved.
- O36 -> L_own_txspayload: REFUTED, replayed on real Go 1.24.7.
- No law: O3-O10, O13, O14, O16-O18, O20, O21, O23-O25, O28-O30, O34, O35, O37.
- D1 -> L_par_hdr_v0 and L_par_hdr_v1 (plus L_rt_go_v0/1/2): PROVED.
- D5 -> L_undo_CSR and L_undo_BD: PROVED.
- D2 is partial. The "oracle-checked HypZ" claim in spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json and docs/M1_REPORT.md has no implementing code.
- No law: D3, D4, D6, D7, D8, D9.
- N1 is done (as O15). N2 is partial (O12, contract missing). N3 (O25) and N4 (O14) are missing.

UNCOVERED ITEMS, GROUPED BY THE MACHINERY THEY NEED:
- (A) Extensions to the existing M1 rollup machine: a proof class for inductive invariants over all actions, the SYM split generators, cost annotations, accounting, and a ghost record of who chose the content. Needed by O20, O25 (FACT part), O30, O32, O35, the external half of O31, O33 minimality, the O12 contract, D4, D6 (rollup part) and D8.
- (B) Migration and initializer facts: importGenesisBatch, initialize3/4 with the reinitializer version, η_enq, η_BVH, the registry cutover, and an IR form for composition coherence. Needed by O9, O13, O14, O16, O17, O18 and O21.
- (C) Messenger, queue and Merkle facts: replayMessage and proveAndRelayMessage, the whitelist fee rule, Verify.sol, and withdrawalRoots. Needed by O29, O34, D6 (messenger part), D7, D9 and part of D8.
- (D) Verifier router and public-input facts, plus a circuit hypothesis HypC. Needed by O3, O23 and O8.
- (E) Go codec facts at loop and array granularity, plus a compression oracle (M2 extraction scope). Needed by O4, O5, O6, O28, O37, D2 and D3.
- (F) Go derivation facts (ParseBatch) and a product machine linking the Solidity commit to Go derivation. Needed by O7, O8, O24, and F11's unmapped "L1 counts discarded" sub-item.
- (G) Intent lane and intent contracts, with gate check G10 (M5). Needed by O10 and O12.
- (H) Bounded games and a realistic cost model (M5). Needed by the economic readings of O25, O35 and O13, and by the O33 cost.
- (I) Outcome vocabulary: split-on-hypothesis, conditional, benign, intended-bounded, and impact. The frozen triage enum lacks these; this is a question for the human.

INTEGRITY AND DEBT:
- laws/M1, spec/M1/predictions.json and whitepaper.md are not in FROZEN.sha256.
- The M1 predictions were first committed together with the M1 results (commit 9a96037).
- holon/mpipeline.py:233 attaches the rollup CF premise to every M1 record, including the Go OWN law.
- The pinned code still seems to show the F11 derivation gaps: leftover transactions are never checked, and the last block number is never compared with the header's lastBlockNumber.
- Whitepaper inconsistencies: no O-id maps F12.5 (downgrade) or F11 "L1 counts discarded", and O18 cites "A15", which is not defined anywhere.

summary:
Short answer: the repo does what M0 and M1 asked for, but almost none of the §12 metrics or the §13 evaluation protocol exists in code. M2 to M5 have essentially not been started. M2's historical-input replay cannot be built in this container as it stands, because the network policy blocks every Ethereum RPC and blob archive.

**What exists and works (checked in the code, not taken from the docs):**
- **Laws and results.** 24 laws are run end to end: 8 for M0 (PAR) and 16 for M1 (UNDO, SORT, DISCH, FACT, SYM, NAT, OWN). Each ends PROVED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with a result record, in `holon/pipeline.py` and `holon/mpipeline.py`.
- **Gate.** It runs GENV, G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G7 and G11 (`holon/gate.py`, CHECK_ORDER).
- **Canaries.** M0 has 16 and M1 has 21; none were accepted (`results/*/gate_report.json`).
- **Second kernel.** BendTT `--verdict` re-checks all 24 proofs.
- **Pinning.** Bend is pinned to 2.0.36 at checkout 2343aec.
- **Replay on the real code.** Witnesses are replayed on Go (`go test`) and Solidity (Foundry). M1 also has a seeded random corpus of 300 traces and 2,432 steps with 0 disagreements (`replay/M1/report.json` refinement).
- **Mutations.** These plant bugs in the facts, not in the real code (`predictions/M0_mutations.json`, `spec/M1/mutations.json`, tests 31 and m1_mutations).
- **Coverage debt.** It is listed by hand in the M1 facts.

**What is missing or different from the whitepaper:**
- **No metrics or reporting module at all.** `grep -ri metric holon/` finds nothing. The only outputs are `summary.json`, `gate_report.json` and `replay/*/report.json`.
- **Gate checks G6, G8, G9 and G10 do not exist.** G6 is only an opt-in test that skips unless `HOLON_REPLAY=1`.
- **G11 checks something weaker than the whitepaper.** It only checks that each LAWS.bend states exactly one law. It does not check that every premise has an inhabitant.
- **The second kernel is not the Lean export the whitepaper describes.** BendTT re-checks what Bend's own front end produced, so a front-end bug would affect both. There is no Lean emitter that works from the law IR.
- **Replay is not native.** The model is compiled from Bend to `.mjs` and run on node. Real Go and Solidity run offline through `go test` and `forge test`. There is no C library, no cgo and no in-process EVM.
- **No automated extraction.** All facts are hand-written.
- **M1 laws and predictions are not hash-frozen.** `laws/M1` is hand-written IR, and `spec/M1/predictions.json` was committed in bfdb5f2, after the mechanization commit 9a96037. Neither appears in `FROZEN.sha256`.
- **None of these exist anywhere:** Reach predicate, evidence calculus, intent contracts or intent lane, hypothesis predicates or split status, rule-gap records, audit loop, blind rerun, STATEMENT_DIFF, stale propagation, performance loop, parallel or GPU checking, games, environment modules.
- **No §13 work.** There is no labelled corpus, no baselines and no ablations.
- **One documented check has no code.** M1_REPORT §5 says the HypZ zero-blob hash was checked against the real oracle, but no code does this.
- **Case-study coverage is partial.** It covers 12 of the 37 obstructions in §11.3 and 2 of the 9 discharged obligations in §11.6.

**What is feasible in this container:**
- **Reachable:** GitHub (git clone of morph-l2/morph at HEAD 3e44e795, the pinned commit, and scroll-tech/scroll), GitHub release downloads (foundry, solc 0.8.24, hevm, echidna), PyPI, npm, crates.io and the Go module proxy.
- **Toolchains:** Bend can emit C, and go, gcc, clang and cargo are installed.
- **Therefore:** extraction (solc AST/Yul, go/ssa), a native C model, cgo, an EVM through revm or Foundry, and the baselines (slither, echidna, hevm, halmos, z3, Go fuzzing) can all be installed and built here.
- **Not feasible: historical on-chain inputs.** All public Ethereum RPCs, the beacon API, blobscan, etherscan and Morph's own RPC and explorer return 403 on CONNECT, a policy denial.
  - BigQuery's API host is reachable, but gcloud has no credentials.
  - The morph repo has only 6 synthetic calldata fixtures (`node/derivation/testdata/rollup_calldata_fixtures.json`, lastBlockNumber 12345).
  - The M2 historical-window exit criterion therefore needs one of three things from the human: a snapshot they supply, GCP credentials, or an egress allow-list change.

items.item: Deterministic translators: Solidity (solc AST / Yul) and Go (go/ssa) codec extraction into facts
items.evidence: No holon/frontends/ directory. `grep -riE 'solc|slither|go/ssa|yul' holon/` finds no extractor. facts/morph_header.json extraction.method = 'hand-written from the audit bundle'. spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json extraction.method = 'hand-written from the real repo at the pinned commit'. `command -v solc` reports MISSING, but the GitHub release solc-static-linux v0.8.24 is reachable (HTTP 206). go 1.24.7 is installed and proxy.golang.org is reachable (200).
items.gap: §10.1 says straight-line Yul and Go-SSA fragments must be translated mechanically, with every unsupported fragment recorded as coverage debt. Today every fact is transcribed by hand, so L1's 'Construction' layer (§12.1) does not exist.
items.proposed_work:
1. Solidity extractor: holon/frontends/solidity/extract.py runs `solc --standard-json` (pinned 0.8.24 from the GitHub release, installed by tools/setup_env.sh). It walks the Yul IR or inline assembly of BatchHeaderCodecV0/V1.store* and Rollup.commitBatch, and emits holon-facts/0.1 layout ops (mstore/mstore8/shl offsets) in the existing facts/morph_header.json op format.
2. Go extractor: holon/frontends/go/cmd/holon-extract/main.go uses golang.org/x/tools/go/ssa to turn binary.BigEndian.PutUint64, constant-offset copy and append chains in common/batch/batch_header.go into the same ops. Unsupported SSA instructions go into a `coverage.debt` list and are never approximated.
3. Determinism: sorted output and no source timestamps.
4. Tests: tests_m2/test_extract.py checks that the extracted facts equal facts/morph_header.json modulo source-reference fields (normalized byte-for-byte). If they differ, the run stops and lists the differences as a facts-audit question; facts/ itself is frozen and must not be edited.
5. G1 then regenerates facts→model→laws from source.

items.item: Automated extraction of straight-line state updates (guards and effects) into the holon-facts/0.2 guarded-command DSL
items.evidence: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json (actions with guards/effects and a source line per guard) is hand-written. holon/gen/machine.py compiles the DSL. docs/M1_REPORT.md §7: 'The facts DSL is the target format extraction must produce'. No extractor exists.
items.gap: M2 requires extracting state machines: external functions become transitions, require and modifiers become guards in source order, storage writes become effects, and loop bounds become cost terms. The rollup slice is hand-modelled.
items.proposed_work:
1. Add holon/frontends/solidity/state.py working from the solc AST (compact JSON) of Rollup.sol and L1MessageQueueWithGasPriceOracle.sol.
2. Emit each external function as an action:
   - guards: `require(cond, reason)`, `if (..) revert`, modifiers inlined, in order, with reason strings mapped to the `reasons` table;
   - effects: storage assignments, as field updates over per-index maps.
3. Only straight-line bodies are supported. Loops and non-straight-line constructs become coverage debt.
4. Validate on the modelled subset: tests_m2/test_state_extract.py diffs the extracted guards and effects for commitBatch, revertBatch, challengeState, proveState and finalizeBatch against spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json (after renaming), then reruns the M1 pipeline on the extracted facts with --no-registry and requires identical summary.json outcomes.
items.depends_on: Solidity translator infrastructure (solc install, AST walker)

items.item: Replay harness: model compiled to a C library, Go via cgo, Solidity on an EVM interpreter or pinned fork
items.evidence: holon/model_eval.py and holon/mpipeline.py CompiledMachine.build compile the model with `bend X.bend -o X.mjs` and evaluate it in node (holon/js/eval.mjs, machine.mjs, explore.mjs). holon/replay.py and holon/mreplay.py instead copy morph's common/ into a scratch workspace and run a hand-written `go test` file (replay/M0/go/holon_replay_test.go, replay/M1/go/holon_own_test.go), or run `forge test` on replay/M1/solidity/HolonTraceReplay.t.sol, and compare log lines afterwards. No C output and no cgo: `grep -rn cgo holon` is empty. `bend --help` shows `-o <out>` can emit C or a binary, so the target exists. forge is currently MISSING in this container (`command -v forge`), and ~/.holon/morph and ~/.holon/foundry are absent. The GitHub foundry release is reachable (206).
items.gap: §8.7 asks for high-throughput differential replay: the native model library and the implementation fed the same inputs in one process. Today's replay is a batch of offline subprocess runs. Throughput is limited to about 2.4k steps per run, there is no per-edge harness, and codec edges (M0) have no corpus replay at all. Re-running replay here also requires `tools/setup_env.sh --replay`.
items.proposed_work:
1. Probe first: add bend/notes/c_probe/ (not a frozen directory) to see whether Bend's C output exposes callable entry points or only `main`.
2. If entry points are exposed: holon/native.py runs `bend gen/<m>/model/<name>.bend -o build/native/<name>.c` and `gcc -O2 -shared` into libholonmodel.so. A Go harness at replay/M2/go/holon_cgo_test.go calls it through cgo and calls common/batch functions directly on the same inputs.
3. Otherwise: compile a model binary with a stdin/stdout JSON protocol and drive it from Go.
4. EVM side, choose one:
   - an in-process revm harness under replay/M2/evm/ (Rust, crates.io is reachable) that loads Rollup bytecode built by solc;
   - keep Foundry, installed through setup_env.sh.
5. Write each edge's agreement counts to results/<m>/refinement/<edge_id>.json.
6. Make sure gate G1 never depends on network or toolchain timing.

items.item: Per-edge replay corpus from all four input sources (grammar samples, sort-boundary values, witnesses, historical)
items.gap: Every edge needs its own replay corpus from all four sources, and refinement records must be attached to the edges that results depend on. None of this exists for codec edges. For the state machine, the corpus has no boundary values and no historical inputs.

items.item: Historical on-chain inputs: past commit calldata and archived blobs replayed through model codecs and compared with stored commitments and node derivations
items.evidence:
No code. `grep -rni historical holon/` matches only text in config/triage.json. Network checks from this container:
